title: test-coverage action does not display testthat output on Windows
description:
**Describe the bug**
On windows, the test-coverage action does not display testthat output.

![image](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/assets/34234913/35c163f9-26e5-47ab-9df6-2eba1724f584)


**To Reproduce**
see: https://github.com/esqLABS/esqlabsR/actions/runs/6970686406/job/18969127187#step:10:17

The action is looking for `D:a_temp/package` which does not exist since the step before ("Test coverage") stores the outputs at `D:/a/_temp/package` (from `file.path(normalizePath(Sys.getenv("RUNNER_TEMP"), winslash = "/"), "package")`)

**Expected behavior**
The action should look for the testthat.Rout file at `D:/a/_temp/package`.

**Additional context**
The problem seems to come from the interpretation of `${{ runner.temp }}/package` in the "Show testthat output" step in a windows context since it results in `D:a_temp/package` instead of `D:/a/_temp/package`.

**Possible fix**
According to this, adding `'` around the path constructor (like this: `'${{ runner.temp }}/package'` solves the issue. I tested it in our repository and it seems to work (see https://github.com/esqLABS/esqlabsR/actions/runs/6971498430/job/18971691010#step:10:1)

title: Install older pandoc will be overwritten by setup-r-dependencies System dependencies installation on Linux
description:
In R Markdown ecosystem we are testing older pandoc version. This may not be a wide usage. 

I was trying to understand why I lost `pandoc-citeproc` availability with 2.73 and 2.5 and it took me time to understand that using `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` will try to install pandoc from Ubuntu repo (which is currently version 2.9.2.1). 

This will make any version installed with `r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2` in a step before to be installed over and make **rmarkdown** use this latest one, which is unexpected. 

Opening this issue to share this problem. Don't know if there could be a solution. Several ideas: 

- not install pandoc in `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` with **pak** if already installed 
- Add as switch to opt-in a removal of Pandoc `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2`

Currently, [our solution](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/2466) is to uninstall Pandoc after `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` and installing manually using the `setup-pandoc` action.

title: Fail to install bioconductor dependencies during check
description:
**Describe the bug**
I have a package that depends on several Bioconductor packages and I want to pass CI checks and to be able to install it. 

When I have only one Bioconductor dependency (e.g. [`limma`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/limma.html)), I need to add a `Remotes` field in `DESCRIPTION` like this: 
```
Remotes:
    bioc::limma
```
Doing this, GHA (`usethis::use_github_action_check_standard()`) works and the package could be installed with `remotes::install_github()`.

However, when I have two Bioconductor dependencies in `Imports`, with one is also a dependency of the other. (e.g. [`affy`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/affy.html) and [`Biobase`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/Biobase.html)), this `Remotes` fields doesn't work:
```
Remotes:
    bioc::affy,
    bioc::Biobase,
    bioc::limma
```
It leads to this error in checks:
```
Error: 
  ! error in pak subprocess
  Caused by error: 
  ! Could not solve package dependencies:
  * deps::.: Can't install dependency bioc::affy
  * bioc::affy: Can't install dependency Biobase (>= 2.5.5)
```

I need to remove `Biobase` from it to make it works (it is still install through `affy`)
```
Remotes:
    bioc::affy,
    bioc::limma
```
This tweak works. 

However, when `affy` is in `Suggests` and `Biobase` in `Imports`, this last `Remotes` field pass GHA but the package can't be installed with `install_github()`. 

**To Reproduce**
I created a test package with several configurations : https://github.com/abichat/test.dep.bioc
This is where the `affy` + `Biobase` failed: https://github.com/abichat/test.dep.bioc/actions/runs/4477072225/jobs/7868146514#step:5:135

**Expected behavior**
I would like to add all Bioconductor dependencies in the Remotes fields, without the tweak of keeping only  "terminal dependency" (which doesn't work in the case of `Suggest`ed packages). 


Thanks!

title: style workflow fails due to lack of repository permissions
description:
I found this issue on a private repo, but set up a dummy repo to test my hypotheses here.  The style action fails with a 403 (forbidden) error:

```
remote: Permission to thisisnic/testingghactions.git denied to github-actions[bot].
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/thisisnic/testingghactions/': The requested URL returned error: 403
Error: Process completed with exit code 128.
```

I believe that the cause of it could be a change in the default permissions that the GITHUB_TOKEN uses from February, which [switched permissions from read/write to read-only](https://github.blog/changelog/2023-02-02-github-actions-updating-the-default-github_token-permissions-to-read-only/).

**Describe the bug**
"Commit and push changes" step of 'style' action fails

**To Reproduce**
Failed build here: https://github.com/thisisnic/testingghactions/actions/runs/6703972117/job/18215481594 

**Expected behavior**
The step successfully pushes changes to the branch

**Additional context**

If I add `write` permissions to the `pull-requests`, this issue persists: https://github.com/thisisnic/testingghactions/actions/runs/6704107978/job/18215883920

If I add `write` permissions to the `contents`, then the job now works: https://github.com/thisisnic/testingghactions/actions/runs/6704148262/job/18216003844

After doing more digging around, this looks like it's basically [the same issue as was fixed for the pkgdown build-and-deploy](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/pull/719) step actually; I'll submit a PR.

title: Add details on `build_args` to handle large vignettes
description:
I wrestled for a while with R CMD check failing on GH actions but succeeding on my machine, due to different arguments to R CMD build. With [Help from Gábor Csárdi](https://community.rstudio.com/t/larger-vignettes-and-r-cmd-check-warnings/178748), I was able to adjust the check-standard.yaml to reproduce the desired, passing test on GH. 

My solution was to replace

```
- uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          args: 'c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")'
```

```
- uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          args: 'c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")'
          build_args: c('--compact-vignettes=gs+qpdf')
```

title: `setup-renv` fails to install internal package in private PPM when `use-public-rspm` is set to `true`
description:
The `setup-renv` action fails to install packages only available from a private Posit Package Manager when the input `use-public-rspm` is set to to `true` in the previous `setup-r` action step. The private PPM is set in the `extra-repositories` input in `setup-r`.

This issue seems to be caused by the automatic setting of `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE` that was introduced in 8079098, which overrides the private PPM repository and uses the PPPM instead, which does not contain the internal package.

An example workflow would look something like this, with the renv.lock file containing an internal package only available in a private PPM:

``` yaml
jobs:
  renv-fail:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true
          extra-repositories: 'https://private-ppm.com/repo/latest'
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**

By default, I would expect `setup-renv` to not override the private PPM where the internal packages are. Is there a way to set `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE` to `NULL` in `setup-renv`?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I guess I could set `use-public-rspm` to `false` and then set the `repos` option manually but I think it makes sense to allow for this workflow within `setup-renv` so that we can easily set the repos in `setup-r` with `use-public-rspm` and `extra-repositories`.

title: setup-r-dependencies ignores `?source` parameter in `extra-packages`
description:
**Describe the bug**
Because of [the issue in Matrix](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-package-devel/2023q4/010051.html), I need to build `lme4` from source in my GHA workflow. According to the README of setup-r-dependencies here at GH and `pak` documentation, I stated this in the `extra-packages` field like this (note that `lme4=?source` failed with an uninformative error):

```yaml
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          extra-packages: |
            any::rcmdcheck
            cran::lme4?source
          needs: check
```

However, `pak` lockfile is created with `lme4` from RPSM binary, ignoring the code above. Note that there was no cache present. Only after introducing `upgrade: 'TRUE'` to the workflow file, `lme4` was installed from source (but the lockfile generated still uses RPSM binary).

**To Reproduce**
Here are the logs for a failed action: [logs_failed.zip](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/files/13365015/logs_failed.zip)
Here are the logs after introducing `upgrade: 'TRUE'`: [logs_ok.zip](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/files/13365155/logs_ok.zip)


**Expected behavior**
`pak` builds a lockfile that reflects `extra-packages`. Note that I mimicked the process on macOS and the lockfile and installation went OK, correctly building `lme4` from source.

title: Failure in `setup-r-dependencies` if `.Rprofile` and `extra-repositories` are present
description:

The `setup-r-dependencies` action fails with an uninformative/misleading error message.

**To Reproduce**

I use [check-standard.yaml](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/v2-branch/examples/check-standard.yaml) workflow with 3 additional things in my project:

1) Additional CRAN-like repository added as `extra-repositories: "https://mokymai.github.io/download/"` (line 42 in [my GHA workflow](https://github.com/GegznaV/tmp1/blob/631104ff70ee7925722db92d85611ad303df14c4/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml#L42C11-L42C68))

![image](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/assets/12725868/1e552371-ea71-421a-a8db-ef5759cb4342)

These 3 conditions cause `setup-r-dependencies` **failure** by not finding package (packages) from the extra repos.

**Expected behavior**
No issues even with `.Rprofile` present.

**Additional context**
To debug the issue I created a temporary GH repo:
https://github.com/GegznaV/tmp1

You may study a few last commits (especially the indicated ones) to understand the issue better
![image](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/assets/12725868/9ab72e83-8f90-4907-95c6-c75579a2b151)

I also add a zip of this repo, in case it gets unavailable:

title: Action Setup-R@v2 changes curl version
description:
Apologies if this is not the right place to ask/mention this, please direct me to a more appropriate place. Recently, some of our CI runs using the setup-r action at version 2 have started to fail and my debugging process has led me to believe this is caused by the setup-r action.

**Describe the bug**
We are running a custom action to setup GAMS on a GitHub runner, which includes [this line](https://github.com/iiasa/actions/blob/ac6cb15c2f918681099a951edb57d03051743cc1/setup-gams/script.sh#L49) `curl https://d37drm4t2jghv5.cloudfront.net/distributions/25.1.1/windows/windows_x64_64.exe --output gams.exe` (simplified for our purposes here). This line fails on some of our runs with this error:
```bash
  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
                                 Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed

  0     0    0     0    0     0      0      0 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:--     0* Host d37drm4t2jghv5.cloudfront.net:443 was resolved.
* IPv6: (none)
* IPv4: 18.160.37.25, 18.160.37.140, 18.160.37.169, 18.160.37.49
*   Trying 18.160.37.25:443...
* Connected to d37drm4t2jghv5.cloudfront.net (18.160.37.25) port 443
* ALPN: curl offers h2,http/1.1
} [5 bytes data]
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
} [512 bytes data]
* error setting certificate file: /usr/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
* error setting certificate file: /usr/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt

  0     0    0     0    0     0      0      0 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:--     0
* Closing connection
* error setting certificate file: /usr/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
* error setting certificate file: /usr/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
curl: (77) error setting certificate file: /usr/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt
```
During debugging, I noticed that this only happens when `curl --version` reads as follows:
```bash
curl 8.5.0 (x86_64-pc-cygwin) libcurl/8.5.0 OpenSSL/3.2.0 zlib/1.3.1 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.5 libidn2/2.3.4 libpsl/0.21.5 (+libidn2/2.3.4) libssh2/1.11.0 nghttp2/1.59.0
Release-Date: 2023-12-06
Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher gophers http https imap imaps mqtt pop3 pop3s rtsp scp sftp smb smbs smtp smtps telnet tftp
Features: alt-svc AsynchDNS brotli GSS-API HSTS HTTP2 HTTPS-proxy IDN IPv6 Kerberos Largefile libz NTLM PSL SPNEGO SSL threadsafe TLS-SRP UnixSockets zstd
```
I was able to notice this because as part of the [same CI workflow](https://github.com/iiasa/message_ix/actions/runs/7786111023/job/21230173440?pr=790), we have other tests running on Windows and `curl`ing the exact same URL successfully. On these runs, `curl --version` yields:
```bash
curl 8.4.0 (x86_64-w64-mingw32) libcurl/8.4.0 Schannel zlib/1.3 brotli/1.1.0 zstd/1.5.5 libidn2/2.3.4 libpsl/0.21.2 (+libidn2/2.3.3) libssh2/1.11.0
Release-Date: 2023-10-11
Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher gophers http https imap imaps ldap ldaps mqtt pop3 pop3s rtsp scp sftp smb smbs smtp smtps telnet tftp
Features: alt-svc AsynchDNS brotli HSTS HTTPS-proxy IDN IPv6 Kerberos Largefile libz NTLM PSL SPNEGO SSL SSPI threadsafe UnixSockets zstd
```
The only real difference between the windows runs (except for a few environment variables being set) is that the "tutorial" run [includes](https://github.com/glatterf42/message_ix/blob/c413c45ed196dc54de0ab3a79e80bd283c98d45f/.github/workflows/pytest.yaml#L172-L173)
```yaml
    - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
      id: setup-r
```
while the non-tutorial run doesn't. And indeed, including a few lines of auxiliary output reveals:
![curl-version-change-in-windows-ci](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/assets/83776373/5639f298-9e8d-4f95-91f6-dff4dae0b868)

**To Reproduce**
Please feel free to push changes to https://github.com/iiasa/actions/tree/debug-setup-gams, which can then be used to trigger another workflow on https://github.com/iiasa/message_ix/pull/790. 
For more information about the GitHub runner image, please find the full logs here: https://github.com/iiasa/message_ix/actions/runs/7786111023/job/21230173440?pr=790

**Expected behavior**
If possible, I'd like the same version of curl to be available after the setup-r action. Especially since the libcurl version before the setup-r action is built [with Schannel support, which is a Windows-native SSL library](https://curl.se/docs/sslcerts.html), which might explain why this version allows our other CI runs to pass.

**Additional context**
Please let me know if there's anything else you need.

title: Artifact name conflict when using check-r-package twice with same OS
description:
In CI workflows for R Markdown and for Quarto R package, I use the same OS twice with same R version but different Pandoc or Quarto version for example. 

With v2 update this leads to conflict in artifact naming

Example of matrix 

````yaml
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release', quarto: 'pre-release'}

          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release', quarto: 'pre-release'}
          - 
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,  r: 'release', quarto: 'pre-release'}
````

Artifact name will not differs as they do not know the other parameter of the matrix 

- `Linux-X64-rrelease-testthat-snapshots` for ubuntu
- `Windows-X64-rrelease-testthat-snapshots` for Windows
- `macOS-X64-rrelease-testthat-snapshots` for Mac

This break the CI using `v2` so I need to revert back to v2.6.5 for now. 

Would it be possible to add a key provided by user in action config that would be appended to the artifact name ? 
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/ab0a542bf033c5fbe8f65834c003312f2d3afba3/check-r-package/action.yaml#L64

For example I could do 

```yaml
      - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          upload-snapshots: true
          artifact-key: ${{ matrix.config.quarto || 'release' }}
```

Hi @gaborcsardi,

Thanks for releasing and maintaining **r-lib/actions** which is very helpful for the community. Recently, I noticed that many R packages on CRAN had delayed r-oldrel (x86_64) macOS binary releases compared to the latest version (e.g. [RSQLite](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RSQLite/index.html)’s r-oldrel (x86_64) was only updated to v2.3.1, yet the current version has already been v2.3.4). There are binary versions available but the source versions are later

Could I ask how to specify in the R GitHub Actions command, such that I can just install the latest **binary** versions (in this case installing binary package RSQLite v2.3.1, instead of installing the latest source package RSQLite v2.3.4), to avoid package dependency issues on R GitHub Actions?

Thank you very much in advance for your help.

title: Optimizing check speed
description:
Hi, 

The more my packages grow big with examples and vignettes, the slower the checking process takes. 
As GH Actions check on multiple platforms, I sometimes reach 1 hour of cumulative CPU time spent.

I imagine there could be several ways to optimize check speed:

1. parallelize different steps across multiple CPUs (I guess most steps are independent from each other)
2. allow additional options for `R CMD check` to be set through environment variables instead of RStudio Build tools project options (so that one can easily switch from a quick no-vignette no-example check to a complete pre-commit check )
3. add helpers to allow checking for only one specific step 
4. think of a tool to find the critical steps where time could be optimized (sorting the steps by timing maybe?)

I could not find any resources about such options, would that be feasible and a reasonable feature request?

title: setup-renv should allow for specifying working-directory
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'm having an renv.lock file in a subdirectory of a larger repo. But the setup-renv action only works when the root directory has the renv.lock file.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Numerous github actions allow to pass a `path` to `with` to specify the working directory. Since `working-directory` only works with `run`, it's not possible to use it in combination with setup-revnv. The desired UX would be:

```yaml
 - name: Setup renv
   uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
   with:
     path: path/to/renv-lock-dir
     cache-version: 2
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I'm currently working around this limitation with a crude hack:

```yaml
- name: Hoist renv.lock
  run: ln -s web/renv.lock
```

(This is still less code than copying out the relevant bits and pieces and handroll the action.)

title: GA renv cache takes a long time to restore
description:
**Describe the bug**
I've successfully created a GA workflow for a "live" dataset (one that is designed to download remote data, process it and commit and push it on a schedule).

I'm using `r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2` as part of it to install R packages from an `.renv.lock`. I understand that this supports GA's caching functionality.

After my first successful run, a cache was created for the workflow. Subsequent runs have reported the following:

<details>
<summary>Run actions/cache@v3</summary>

```
Run actions/cache@v3
  with:
    path: /home/runner/work/_temp/renv
    key: Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS-R version 4.3.1 (2023-06-16)-1-f07bb93ddaef954c8a486a3e0909a5cfe16cd20f0ac1932f0ec2f10ac31e6ff8
    restore-keys: Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS-R version 4.3.1 (2023-06-16)-1-
    enableCrossOsArchive: false
    fail-on-cache-miss: false
    lookup-only: false
  env:
    GITHUB_PAT: ***
    R_LIBS_USER: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library
    TZ: UTC
    _R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_: FALSE
    NOT_CRAN: true
    RENV_PATHS_ROOT: /home/runner/work/_temp/renv
Received 37748736 of 219609757 (17.2%), 35.9 MBs/sec
Received 138412032 of 219609757 (63.0%), 65.9 MBs/sec
Received 219609757 of 219609757 (100.0%), 78.3 MBs/sec
Cache Size: ~209 MB (219609757 B)
/usr/bin/tar -xf /home/runner/work/_temp/fc14cec1-f[69](https://github.com/360-info/tracker-ocean-temperatures/actions/runs/5747629298/job/15578982394#step:5:73)0-457d-b50a-9d9d8cc6b32e/cache.tzst -P -C /home/runner/work/tracker-ocean-temperatures/tracker-ocean-temperatures --use-compress-program unzstd
Cache restored successfully
Cache restored from key: Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS-R version 4.3.1 (2023-06-16)-1-f07bb93ddaef954c8a4[86](https://github.com/360-info/tracker-ocean-temperatures/actions/runs/5747629298/job/15578982394#step:5:91)a3e0909a5cfe16cd20f0ac1932f0ec2f10ac31e6ff8
```

</details>

Looks successful! I'm not saving any time, though—the `setup-renv` takes about 33 minutes regardless of whether I get a message about the cache successfully being used. This is actually about 25% slower than downloading and installing the packages from source.

I'm not sure if this is actually the caching itself—on runs where the cache is successfully used, I observe the log getting stuck on the previous step for nearly the whole half hour:

<details>
<summary>Run cat("os-version=", sessionInfo()$running, "\n", file = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OUTPUT"), sep = "", append = TRUE)</summary>

```
Run cat("os-version=", sessionInfo()$running, "\n", file = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OUTPUT"), sep = "", append = TRUE)
  cat("os-version=", sessionInfo()$running, "\n", file = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OUTPUT"), sep = "", append = TRUE)
  cat("r-version=", R.Version()$version.string, "\n", file = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OUTPUT"), sep = "", append = TRUE)
  shell: /usr/local/bin/Rscript {0}
  env:
    GITHUB_PAT: ***
    R_LIBS_USER: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library
    TZ: UTC
    _R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_: FALSE
    NOT_CRAN: true
    RENV_PATHS_ROOT: /home/runner/work/_temp/renv
```

I'm not sure if this means that there is a previous step the action gets stuck on, or if this is the last thing output before it gets stuck with the caching, and the caching action log just doesn't appear until it's complete. But when the cache isn't used, I see my R packages slowly but consistently logging their download and installation messages over the course of half an hour.

</details>

**To Reproduce**
Here's the workflow log: https://github.com/360-info/tracker-ocean-temperatures/actions/workflows/ingest-monthly.yml

Here's the workflow code (on the `dryrun-monthly` branch): https://github.com/360-info/tracker-ocean-temperatures/blob/dryrun-monthly/.github/workflows/ingest-monthly.yml

**Expected behavior**
I was hoping that a successful cache load would take less than a minute, saving me substantial time on instances when I find that there isn't any new data to download.

title: Detect "Additional_repositories:" in DESCRIPTION file
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
In my DESCRIPTION file (of my R package), I can specify `Additional_repositories:` for the r-universe repository where one of my dependencies is found. I can edit my workflows, to include `extra-repositories` for the `set-r` action, but it'd be nice if `set-r` detected the `Additional_repositories:` line in my DESCRIPTION file.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
One of two solutions:
* `set-r` detects the `Additional_repositories:` line in my DESCRIPTION file and adds that to `extra-dependencies`
* `setup-r-dependencies` detects it and has a `pak::repo_add()` line so `pak` finds it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I can totally add it to my GitHub workflows myself but I have many of these. Also it took awhile to figure out why the package builds fine on `rhub` (in prep for a CRAN release), but my workflow was failing.

Also with `r-universe` becoming more popular, more people might run into this same issue.

title: setup-r / setup-pandoc stuck on macOS (hitting 6h timeout)
description:
**Describe the bug**
Over the last weeks, I have often seen setup-r (and setup-pandoc, just today) getting stuck and eventually hitting the default 6h timeout.
This has happened on macOS-latest, in different repos and for various R versions.
From the log it is not very clear where and why the execution got stuck (especially for setup-r), and the issue is transient in that a re-run usually goes through.

**To Reproduce**

Examples of failures, with relevant logs including timing for convenience  and for the records:

- rmdgallery, setup-r, macOS-latest (devel): https://github.com/riccardoporreca/rmdgallery/runs/3981690523?check_suite_focus=true
```
Sat, 23 Oct 2021 00:51:51 GMT ==> Pouring qpdf--10.3.2.big_sur.bottle.tar.gz

```

- rmdgallery, setup-r, macOS-latest (oldrel-1): https://github.com/riccardoporreca/rmdgallery/runs/3997956955?check_suite_focus=true
```
Mon, 25 Oct 2021 14:07:22 GMT ==> Pouring qpdf--10.3.2.big_sur.bottle.tar.gz
Mon, 25 Oct 2021 14:07:27 GMT 🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/qpdf/10.3.2: 73 files, 6.3MB
Mon, 25 Oct 2021 14:07:27 GMT ==> Pouring checkbashisms--2.21.4.all.bottle.tar.gz
Mon, 25 Oct 2021 14:07:32 GMT 🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/checkbashisms/2.21.4: 6 files, 71.2KB
Mon, 25 Oct 2021 20:06:43 GMT Error: The operation was canceled.
```

- rTRNG, setup-r, macOS-latest (oldrel): https://github.com/miraisolutions/rTRNG/runs/4123058504?check_suite_focus=true
```
Sat, 06 Nov 2021 00:14:44 GMT ==> Pouring qpdf--10.3.2.big_sur.bottle.tar.gz
Sat, 06 Nov 2021 00:14:48 GMT 🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/qpdf/10.3.2: 73 files, 6.3MB

Sat, 06 Nov 2021 00:14:51 GMT 🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/checkbashisms/2.21.4: 6 files, 71.2KB
Sat, 06 Nov 2021 06:14:12 GMT Error: The operation was canceled.
```

- rTRNG, setup-pandoc, macOS-latest (release): https://github.com/miraisolutions/rTRNG/runs/4195770215?check_suite_focus=true

**Expected behavior**
It would be great if setup-r and setup-pandoc would capture explicitly the issue causing the action to get stuck, or perhaps just handle a meaningful timeout internally for individual operations, perhaps hinting at re-running the workflow in a timeout error message.

**Additional context**
Given how common the issue is (I see it every week in cron runs), it is not great to keep a runner busy for 6hours if we can prevent it.

title: Using setup-r-dependencies correctly
description:
I would open this up in a discussion if I could, but this repo doesn't have this option. Hopefully, it is okay to discuss this here. 

I am experimenting with using Github actions to build and deploy a blog that uses Quarto. As part of the workflow file, I add in this chunk of code because I need these R projects in order to render everything correctly.

```
- name: Add R deps

          cache-version: 2

            any::jsonlite
            any::ggplot2

            any::tinytex
            any::rmarkdown
            any::DiagrammeR
            any::reticulate
            any::lubridate
            any::quarto
```

However, this takes a long time, roughly 10 minutes. This workflow file runs every time I want to update the blog.

title: Allow RSPM to fallback to CRAN?
description:
RSPM has a delay of a few days for builds to appear and it causes problems attempting to install a package that has just been updated. I'm wondering if it's possible to add a parameter in `setup-r` that controls whether or not RSPM will override CRAN here:

https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/ac4564fd0531646b1471781c2d4cdf83704cabf8/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L541-L545

For context, I first spotted this in https://github.com/carpentries/actions/issues/69 and determined that it's part of https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1147.

title: Document workflow fails when `RoxygenNote:` is out of date in the `DESCRIPTION`
description:
**Describe the bug**
Document workflow can modify the DESCRIPTION file (by updating the Roxygen version note) but it won't commit the change. This leads to a build error when there is nothing else to commit.

**To Reproduce**
[failed build](https://github.com/Public-Health-Scotland/phsopendata/runs/8211178309?check_suite_focus=true)

Run the action on a package which is 'properly' documented but has an older roxygen version in the DESCRIPTION

**Expected behaviour**
Commit the change to the DESCRIPTION. Or do nothing but don't fail if only the DESCRIPTION is to be changed.

title: style does not commit changes made to `.R` files in `tests/`
description:
**Describe the bug**
The style workflow does not commit any styled changes made to R scripts in the `tests/` folder (even though styler is run against these with `styler::style_pkg()`). This results in an error when the tests are the only files styled, as styler makes the changes but then nothing is committed.

**To Reproduce**
[failed build](https://github.com/Public-Health-Scotland/phsopendata/runs/8211178304?check_suite_focus=true)

**Expected behavior**
Style changes to the test scripts should also be committed.

title: Installing R 4.3.0 does not find libgcc_s.1.dylib
description:
Apologies if this is not the right place to ask this, but our R tests on macOS have started failing yesterday and I think that's due to a change in the R version that r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2 installs.

**Describe the bug**
The actual error message is as follows:
```
----------------------------- Captured stderr call -----------------------------
java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError: /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.16/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ixmp/backend/jdbc/libgmdjni64.dylib: dlopen(/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.16/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ixmp/backend/jdbc/libgmdjni64.dylib, 0x0001): Library not loaded: '@rpath/libgcc_s.1.dylib'
  Referenced from: '/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.16/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ixmp/backend/jdbc/libgmdjni64.dylib'
  Reason: tried: '/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.16/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ixmp/backend/jdbc/./libgcc_s.1.dylib' (no such file), '/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.9.16/x64/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ixmp/backend/jdbc/./libgcc_s.1.dylib' (no such file), '/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Java_Temurin-Hotspot_jdk/8.0.362-9/x64/Contents/Home/jre/lib/server/./libgcc_s.1.dylib' (no such file), '/Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Java_Temurin-Hotspot_jdk/8.0.362-9/x64/Contents/Home/jre/lib/server/../libgcc_s.1.dylib' (no such file), '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib/libgc
	at java.lang.ClassLoader$NativeLibrary.load(Native Method)
	at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibrary0(ClassLoader.java:1934)
	at java.lang.ClassLoader.loadLibrary(ClassLoader.java:1817)
	at java.lang.Runtime.load0(Runtime.java:782)
	at java.lang.System.load(System.java:1100)
	at com.gams.api.gmd.<clinit>(gmd.java:202)
	at com.gams.api.GAMSDatabase.createGMDObject(GAMSDatabase.java:342)
	at com.gams.api.GAMSDatabase.initializeAttributes(GAMSDatabase.java:328)
	at com.gams.api.GAMSDatabase.<init>(GAMSDatabase.java:256)
	at com.gams.api.GAMSWorkspace.addDatabase(GAMSWorkspace.java:1024)
	at com.gams.api.GAMSWorkspace.addDatabase(GAMSWorkspace.java:1010)
	at at.ac.iiasa.ixmp.objects.Scenario.makeGamsDB(Scenario.java:1812)
	at at.ac.iiasa.ixmp.objects.Scenario.toGDX(Scenario.java:1786)
```
However, there is nothing we deliberately changed on the weekend. Since we are testing on a matrix, we know that all and only the builds for macOS failed (all meaning for all python versions). They all failed while testing R code, so I went back and checked the action that setup R. And indeed, there is a change in the setup from our last successful test to the failing ones. On the successful runs, 'Downloading R' runs `/usr/bin/sudo installer -allowUntrusted -dumplog -pkg /Users/runner/work/_temp/R-4.2.3.pkg -target /`, while on the new failed runs, the corresponding command is `/usr/bin/sudo installer -allowUntrusted -dumplog -pkg /Users/runner/work/_temp/R-4.3.0-x86_64.pkg -target /`.

**To Reproduce**
Please find the logs of our [last successful build here](https://github.com/iiasa/ixmp/actions/runs/4771025097/jobs/8482697386), and the logs of [a current failed build here](https://github.com/iiasa/ixmp/actions/runs/4782653717/jobs/8502185747). Please also find [our workflow file](https://github.com/iiasa/ixmp/actions/runs/4783492472/workflow) and note that it didn't change over the weekend. 
Using e.g. `macos-latest` and python 3.10, we run 
```
- uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
  id: setup-r
```
This then triggers the action with the following arguments:
```
  with:
    r-version: release
    Ncpus: 1
    remove-openmp-macos: true
    http-user-agent: default
    install-r: true
    windows-path-include-rtools: true
    windows-path-include-mingw: true
    update-rtools: false
    use-public-rspm: false
  env:
    depth: 100
    pythonLocation: /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.11/x64
    PKG_CONFIG_PATH: /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.11/x64/lib/pkgconfig
    Python_ROOT_DIR: /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.11/x64
    Python2_ROOT_DIR: /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.11/x64
    Python3_ROOT_DIR: /Users/runner/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.10.11/x64
```

**Expected behavior**
We expect our R code to pass the tests as it does in the logs of the last successful build provided above.

**Additional context**
I've tried looking at a [changelog of R](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/NEWS.pdf) myself, but that didn't yield much success. In [the general version information](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/), I found that R 4.3.0 is supposed to work with XCode 14.2/14.3 and gfortran 12.2. I couldn't find any mention of XCode in our R-related setup jobs, but gfortran is installed as part of the step 'Downloading gfortran' of r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2, where the following command is run: `/usr/bin/sudo hdiutil attach /Users/runner/work/_temp/gfortran-8.2-Mojave.dmg`. Maybe all that's needed to fix this issue is to get the action to install gfortran 12.2?
I'm aware that as a quick fix, we could probably use `r-version` to specify one that is working, but that won't be a sustainable solution.

title: Mis-match in g++ version used for windows devel
description:
**Describe the bug**
When compiling a package for CRAN's windows devel version, there are errors that come up using the windows-builder service and not in the action itself. I've traced this down to the CRAN devel version on Windows using g++ 12.2, whereas r-lib seems to be using the base version of g++ for ubuntu ( likely 11 ). As a result, I am passing checks on my actions, but failing when I try to send it to CRAN.

**To Reproduce**
1 - Clone this repository at this commit. I apologize for not making a minimum viable example; I might be able to get to it but I wanted to know if I am mis-using r-lib's actions somehow: https://github.com/josherrickson/rlemon/commit/b71d6f5fcc5b198342e183baec315026f2f890ca
2 - Make a build using `make build`, and upload to CRAN's windows-builder service. 
3 - Note that our actions, which follow the example, seem to indicate no issues on windows-devel, but do have issues on the builder here: https://win-builder.r-project.org/S2lW0e0aGrn9/00install.out. ( If this is gone by the time a contributor reads this it's `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` type errors.

**Expected behavior**
I expect that, when using these actions, they perform the same checks CRAN uses, so I can be 100% certain that my package is ready ahead of anything else. Alternatively, I just want some way to specify the g++ version, so I can make this change on my own end.


**Additional context**
If this is a bad issue feel free to let me know and close it - I can move this somewhere else, but nothing on the documentation end seems to point to resolving this.

I can solve this by setting `error-on: "'error'"`, but this seems like a poor solution, since I'll miss any other warnings that I actually want to catch. title: Windows builds failing with `DLL 'purrr' not found` error
description:

> DLL 'purrr' not found: maybe not installed for this architecture?

Example [log](https://github.com/r-lib/styler/actions/runs/3772046931/jobs/6412764745) from `{styler}` for Windows R 4.1.

How to avoid such failures? Do I just need to delete the cache?

title: Provide a way to download the latest version of Pandoc
description:
I prefer to always use the latest released version of Pandoc, and my current way of doing this is my hard-coding the version number.

```yaml
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2
        with:
          pandoc-version: "2.19.2"
```

But this is, of course, suboptimal since I manually need to keep updating the version number. 

Instead, I was wondering if it would be possible to use some sentinel value, like the following (which currently [doesn't work](https://github.com/IndrajeetPatil/second-hardest-cs-thing/pull/7)):

```yaml
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2
        with:
          pandoc-version: release
```

This is similar to how one can install the latest pre-release version of [Quarto](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-actions/tree/main/setup): 

```yaml
      - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
        with:
          version: pre-release
```

title: Allow fully disabling cache for local workflow testing
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The current versions of `setup-renv` and friends utilize GitHub cache, which is great, but is incompatible with local testing environments such as [act](https://github.com/nektos/act). This makes local workflow iteration challenging. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

An option to disable the cache step completely as opposed to simply cache invalidation.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Forking the action. ;) 

**Additional context**

ACT sets an environment variable (ACT) to TRUE when running locally. This is one generally recommended way of having skipping GitHub-specific steps for local testing.

cat("LOGNAME=", Sys.info()[["user"]], "\n", sep = "", file = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_ENV"), append = TRUE)

title: TeX packages for building documentation
description:
First of all, thank you so much for these awesome actions. They've helped immensely transition over to GH actions from Travis.

I've noticed a bit of instability with what TeX packages end up being installed when using the `setup-tinyetex` action. After reading the source, I found that by default TinyTeX is installing the list of packages at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yihui/tinytex/master/tools/pkgs-custom.txt and it looks like the oberdiek package has been changed and no longer includes `kvoptions` and `pdftexcmds` (among others) https://ctan.org/ctan-ann/id/mailman.1835.1575146287.2586.ctan-ann@ctan.org

I've also submitted [an issue to TinyTeX](https://github.com/yihui/tinytex/issues/158) to resolve this up stream, but in the interim, I forked this repo and added [an explicit check/install](https://github.com/jonkeane/actions/blob/tiny-tex-additions/setup-tinytex/src/setup-tinytex.ts#L106-L116) of all of the packages I've found necessary in the manual creation process. I'm happy to submit a PR for this, though if it's resolved in TinyTeX it's not strictly necessary any more.  

I've made an incredibly minimal (and useless!) package to show the issue at https://github.com/jonkeane/simple-package see the error in the action around https://github.com/jonkeane/simple-package/runs/329317228#step:7:71 The setup-tinytex stage completes fine, but when R CMD check is run, the manual isn't able to be built because it can't find pdftexcmds.sty

title: YAML folds seem to not be parsed correctly
description:
**Describe the bug**
The `check-full.yaml` workflow has YAML fold block notation on some `run` statements, which don't seem to be parsed correctly. With the folds:

```yaml  
run: >
  Rscript 
    -e "install.packages('remotes')" 
    -e "saveRDS(remotes::dev_package_deps(dependencies = TRUE), 'depends.Rds', version = 2)"
```
Rscript does not receive the `-e` arguments and thus expects a file, which is does not receive.

**To Reproduce**
Create a new repository with [the most recent `check-full.yaml` workflow](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/8b9c40f9254545883fdbba25e279491ccc7c2f6d/examples/check-full.yaml) and let the workflow run. The workflow should fail at the "Query dependencies" stage ([example run logs](https://github.com/Global-TIES-for-Children/rddi/runs/432701773)). Output should be the Rscript usage statements and an error:

```
Usage: /path/to/Rscript [--options] [-e expr [-e expr2 ...] | file] [args]

--options accepted are
  --help              Print usage and exit
  --version           Print version and exit
  --verbose           Print information on progress
  --default-packages=list
                      Where 'list' is a comma-separated set
                        of package names, or 'NULL'
or options to R, in addition to --slave --no-restore, such as
  --save              Do save workspace at the end of the session
  --no-environ        Don't read the site and user environment files
  --no-site-file      Don't read the site-wide Rprofile
  --no-init-file      Don't read the user R profile
  --restore           Do restore previously saved objects at startup
  --vanilla           Combine --no-save, --no-restore, --no-site-file
                        --no-init-file and --no-environ

'file' may contain spaces but not shell metacharacters
Expressions (one or more '-e <expr>') may be used *instead* of 'file'
See also  ?Rscript  from within R
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

**Expected behavior**
The workflow should run as if the run commands were written in a single line ([example workflow success](https://github.com/Global-TIES-for-Children/rddi/runs/432749368) with [single line revisions](https://github.com/Global-TIES-for-Children/rddi/commit/80052589de63ef8fb87cd6aba961906edb1a9017))

**Additional context**
I decided to open an issue because `usethis` pulls from these example scripts, which would be causing downstream workflow failures.

title: Order of steps for check-full workflow
description:
I think there is an issue with the logic of the steps in the [check full workflow](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/check-full.yaml) which prevents the caching feature from being used. 

The `depends.Rds` gets created before the caching step. That means that even during a run where a cache gets restored, the `depends.Rds` gets created against an empty library.

Here is a sample output I see on the `depends.Rds` in a run where there is a cache available

``` 
Needs update -----------------------------
 package      installed available is_cran remote
 clisymbols   NA        1.2.0     TRUE    CRAN  
 crayon       NA        1.3.4     TRUE    CRAN  
 digest       NA        0.6.23    TRUE    CRAN  
 dplyr        NA        0.8.4     TRUE    CRAN  
 glue         NA        1.3.1     TRUE    CRAN  
 httr         NA        1.4.1     TRUE    CRAN  
 jsonlite     NA        1.6.1     TRUE    CRAN  
 knitr        NA        1.28      TRUE    CRAN  
 kableExtra   NA        1.1.0     TRUE    CRAN  
 purrr        NA        0.3.3     TRUE    CRAN  
 readr        NA        1.3.1     TRUE    CRAN 
``` 

Notice the `NA` in the `installed` column.


Because this `depends.Rds` gets used in the 'install dependencies' step, all the packages get installed regardless of whether or not they have been restored in the library from the cache.

A possible solution would be to replace in https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/e85841c5d5b7ae0c0f87782303e5e1f633d40efb/examples/check-full.yaml#L66 `depends.Rds` with another call to `remotes::dev_package_deps(dependencies = TRUE)`

title: /reprex issue trigger
description:
I think a `/reprex` trigger would be useful, similar to `/document` and `/style` in `pr-commands.yaml`.

In the pkgdown repo, we are asking for a reprex more often to debug obscure issues, and it would be nice to provide some consistency to these messages.

A `/reprex` trigger would:

- Answer the issue with some stock language, politely asking for the user to create reprex and explaining why.
- Possibly link to a particularly useful issue where a reprex has been helpful in the past.
- Point the user to instructions on creating a reprex, similar to what we have in the [pkgdown CONTRIBUTING guide](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/dev/CONTRIBUTING.html).
- Add a reprex label to the issue.

title: About using binaries vs. installing from source
description:
Hi Jim,

thanks a lot for the effort in getting GH actions to work easily for R packages. Just browsed your rstudio::conf slides.

We are in the process to support GH actions also in {tic}, building on your "actions".

I see that your are putting in a lot of effort to move towards using R package binaries, even on Linux.
While this comes with a nice speed up for dependency installation, it comes with the issues of R packages which need to link against a system library.
Let's use {rJava} as the best example here ;)

I am wondering if using binaries might introduce more problems in CI than it helps - and if using source installs only (even on Windows) combined with caching the R user library might be the more robust way for most users.
However, installing certain system libs on Windows is of course a medium pain and that's also one reason why binaries exist.
If one wants to test on R-devel, source is the only option anyways.
Also I also like the idea of having the same "build process" for the dep installs across all platforms and pulling away the pain of thinking about binary/source differences at all.

Curious about your view on this.

title: Using the "release" alias results in the wrong rtools tool chain being installed on windows
description:
First, thank you so much for all of the work y'all have put in to these actions they make CI on github actions so very nice. I'm not certain this is a bug that needs to be changed per se, but it took me enough digging to figure out what was going on and the possible reasoning behind it that I want to get this information into an issue in case others are suffering the same problems I was.

When using the `"release"` alias on windows, since #85 rtools was installing the rtools40 toolchain and subsequently, installing packages requiring rtools from source [would not succeed](https://github.com/jonkeane/simple-package/runs/612509766?check_suite_focus=true#step:4:38). I've switched my builds to use the explicit version for the current release and everything is back to green.

It took me a while to realize what was going on here, but ultimately I did see that this was [discussed as part](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/pull/85#issuecomment-616219701) of #85 .

As part of testing this and figuring it out, I made a fork of r-lib/actions to see if it was possible to use the new rtools set up with a `"release"` alias: https://github.com/r-lib/actions/compare/master...jonkeane:release_rtools Though this works, given [the discussion](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/26#issuecomment-567524058) in #26 I suspect this might not be the right approach if the "release" alias should be avoided. I'm happy to also try and send a PR that warns that the "release" alias should be avoided which might prevent others from running into this.

**TL;DR**
If you—like me—were using `"release"` as an alias for the current version of R on Windows and are getting errors referencing rtools when building packages from source, try changing to the recommended method of using the explicit version number (e.g. `"3.6"`) instead of the alias.

title: Enable cache clear by adding a version prefix to the key

> Tip: Caches are immutable so it is useful to start all your cache keys with a version prefix, for example `v1-....` This enables you to regenerate all of your caches by incrementing the version in this prefix. 
(https://circleci.com/docs/2.0/caching/#clearing-cache)

[here](https://github.com/UBESP-DCTV/covid19ita/pull/62/checks?check_run_id=595253618) (pass for R3.5 but not for R3.6), or [here](https://github.com/UBESP-DCTV/covid19ita/runs/595253631?check_suite_focus=true) (pass for R3.6 but not for R3.5), and [here](https://github.com/UBESP-DCTV/covid19ita/pull/62/checks?check_run_id=595523293) (where the missing badge is no more the AppVeyor one but the CodeCov one).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Avoid random errors in CI caused by setting or configuration of CI itself.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
IMO the issue is related to the fact that in the very moment `R CMD check` tray to investigate `README.md` some badge (AppVeyor in the first two examples, CodeCov in the last) are changing and not ready.

Once managed to exclude completely Travis and AppVeyor form the automatic checks (and corresponding badges from the `README`), the only source of the problem can be CodeCov.

Usually, if someone considers to include `covr:codecov()` they include some sort of CI too. Moreover, it can have not that much sense to run it if some checks fail.

[My solution](https://github.com/UBESP-DCTV/covid19ita/blob/action-fix/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml#L93) was to include `covr:codecov()` at the end of the workflow conditionally to the previous success.

I am not sure it is a good idea to include it in the CMD checks template, but suggests somehow to don't use both CMD check and coverage template separately in the same project (maybe by the corresponding helpers in `{usethis}`).


**Additional context**
I have discussed it [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/61268381/windows-r-cmd-check-top-level-files-readme-warning-this-document-format-req/61273758#61273758) too.


PS: thank you to have created those templates!

title: Bioconductor-friendly R CMD check action feature suggestion
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The current https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/check-standard.yaml is not ideal for Bioconductor packages. R and BioC have slightly different release schedules so right now (just before R 4.0.0 and Bioconductor 3.11 are released) using macOS with R-devel is not fully compatible (example, installing dependencies can fail due to system dependency issues). Others have mentioned issues with devel builds (though really R 4.0.0 is `alpha` as R-devel is 4.1). In any case, it's complicated (was for me) to adapt the `check-standard.yml` for Bioconductor packages, which would make these tools less widely used. I recently was also only able to reproduce an error in the Bioconductor machines using their dockers ([story here](https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/bioc-devel/2020-April/016532.html)).

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Bioconductor maintains dockers that have all the required system dependencies installed. I have spent time the last two days adapting https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/check-standard.yaml to use the Bioconductor dockers, run `BiocCheck`, build a deploy a `pkgdown` website, and in theory (I haven't fully tested this) work for both bioc-devel (master git branch) and bioc-release branches (RELEASE_3_10 git branch right now) without having to modify the action `yml` file each release cycle. This action only really runs on `linux`, though it needs one for step to be fully compatible with  https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/check-standard.yaml in case a developer wants to also test using the Windows and macOS R versions provided by `r-lib`.

Overall, I would like this action to be easy to use using `usethis`, which in turns involves `r-lib/actions/examples`.  Related to this, I also would like to suggest tweaking `usethis::use_tidy_support()` (maybe `use_bioc_support()`) as well as `styler::tidyverse_style()`. 

Specific to `r-lib/actions`, at https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/bfe6e309fc13c219dfd8f6616a681013 I copied the contents of https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/check-standard.yaml  into a file named `check-bioc.yaml` and updated it with the current version of the file I have been working on from https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/.github/workflows/check-bioc.yml (has full version history). At https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/bfe6e309fc13c219dfd8f6616a681013/revisions you can see the changes.

The changes are:

* Comments with some links I found useful
* Enable `RELEASE_*` branches
* Find the Bioconductor version from the git branch name and determine which Bioconductor docker to use.
* Pass the `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` to `GITHUB_PAT` for later use.
* Use the Bioconductor docker (if this could become conditional on the `matrix.config.r == 'biocdocker'` then the same workflow could be used for testing on the r-lib R versions too).
* If using `biocdocker`, skip the `r-lib/actions/setup-r` and `setup-pandoc` actions since those are provided by the Bioconductor docker.
* Link a directory in the runner to the docker image, such that R packages can be cached.
* Cache the R packages (Ahh, I need to fix one `if == 'Linux'` and revert it back to `!= 'Windows'`).
* Install `BiocCheck` and copy the files when on `biocdocker` to a path that will enable it to work later.
* Use the BioC options for `rcmdcheck`.
* Run `BiocCheck`.
* Install and run `covr` and `pkgdown` (similar to what you have, just with some extra `git config` statements since we are on the docker linux, not the runner one).

Before I make any PRs, I wanted to mention this plan. I'll do the same for `usethis`, `styler`, and `BiocCheck()` since what I have in mind for those packages is related to this.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

At https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/01_setup.R and https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/02_update.R I have commands that do most of what I want. But they are not shared so easily and could confuse others.

Another alternative is to submit this action to https://github.com/seandavi/BiocActions but this repo is more active, and updates for `check-standard.yaml` would also apply to my proposed `check-bioc.yaml` so it seems best to host the GHA workflow here. Plus `usethis::use_github_action()` defaults to this repo.

**Additional context**

* https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/actions
* https://github.com/LieberInstitute/recount3/actions
* https://gist.github.com/lcolladotor/bfe6e309fc13c219dfd8f6616a681013#file-check-bioc-yaml-L1-L13 particularly https://github.com/seandavi/BiocActions/blob/master/.github/workflows/main.yml and https://github.com/csoneson/dreval/blob/master/.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml. 
* Bioconductor Developer's forum from 2020-04-16 and on the #developers-forum channel in the BioC slack.

title: Skip-ci
description:
I wonder if it could be a good idea to add the possibility to skip CI with keywords in the default R-CMD-check templates. This could be done in one line, like this ([source](https://github.community/t5/GitHub-Actions/GitHub-Actions-does-not-respect-skip-ci/td-p/42834#)):

```
jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    if: "!contains(github.event.head_commit.message, 'skip ci')"
    runs-on: ...
```

It is a useful feature already present on other CI services and users could struggle to find the correct syntax #11 

Thanks

I was helping a colleague set up Actions for his package at the end of the day yesterday, and I am just returning to work today to find that some `R CMD check` jobs ran for 6 hours each overnight. This was a private repo, so the minutes were billable.

title: Ubuntu images for R 4.0 and higher should have checkbashisms script
description:
If a package has a configure or cleanup script, `R CMD check --as-cran` on R 4.0 needs the `checkbashisms` script to be available. For example:

```
* checking top-level files ... WARNING
##[warning]A complete check needs the 'checkbashisms' script.
See section ‘Configure and cleanup’ in the ‘Writing R Extensions’
manual.
```

https://github.com/r-lib/later/pull/121/checks?check_run_id=728590955#step:10:51


This can be installed with `apt-get install devscripts`. See https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker/issues/365.

title: Examples should use --as-cran only for R-release
description: In https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/31a89357c802bbd7843407721c334792ed1e3ff8/examples/check-full.yaml#L84, it uses `--as-cran` for all versions of R, but it's only really needed for the current release version of R, since that's what CRAN uses. Using `--as-cran` for all versions also is slower, and because it traverses URLs in NEWS.md and README.md files, it could cause the servers to start returning errors due to rate limiting.

title: "r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1" action can't recognize the the right R version which **r-oldrel** corresponds to
description:
When we use the "**r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1**" action to setup R environments with different R versions, the action always fails if set **r-version** to be "**oldrel**".

Generally, the R version "**oldrel**" (**r-oldrel**) is the latest version of the previous minor version.
It seems that this action does not recognize the right R version which **r-oldrel** corresponds to, and causes failure to setup the R environment.

We also tested with the version "**release**" (**r-release**), the action can recognize the right R version for **r-release** and setup the R environment successfully.

The following is the workflow I was testing: https://github.com/ForksForTest/TestSetupR/actions/runs/144684310/workflow
You can see the action was failure on all the OSs when **r-version** was **oldrel**, but success when **r-version** was **release**.

Please fix this issue so that the **setup-r** action can recognize the right R version for **r-oldrel**.

title: Windows 'oldrel' installs wrong Rtools
description:
When using `r: 3.6` on Windows, then Rtools35 is installed, which is correct. However when using `r: oldrel` then it installs rtools40, which is incorrect.

https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/b0639fdbe86a288159d72c3c52051d6a5fa392c7/setup-r/src/setup-r.ts#L10-L12

The problem is that we simply test if `r` starts with `"3"`. This worked when I implemented it, because then we did not support `oldrel` yet (and the plan was to keep it that way). So we only had to consider numbered versions and `"devel"`.

I think the solution is to wrap the above in `determineVersion()` ?

title: pr-fetch fails if PR is coming from master branch
description:
**Describe the bug**
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/pr-fetch/src/main.ts#L32 checks out locally the branch of the PR, using the same branch name as on the PR. This is usually fine, but if someone is making a PR from `theirfork/master`, it fails because `master` already exists locally, at least if you've run `actions/checkout` first and that's your default branch too. 

**To Reproduce**
https://github.com/apache/arrow/runs/908154585?check_suite_focus=true

It should not fail to checkout the PR branch.

IDK if anyone relies on the name of the local branch name; if not, seems like it would be simple enough to call the local branch something else guaranteed to be safe. Prepending `pr-` to the branch name, or `username-`, or something could work, or even a random string.

title: 10x price difference between MacOS and Linux runners
description:
I was just looking at GitHub Action's pricing model and was surprised to find out that currently the MacOS runners are charged at 10x the rate of the linux runners, cutting the 2000 minute monthly free credit to 200 minutes. (https://help.github.com/en/github/setting-up-and-managing-billing-and-payments-on-github/about-billing-for-github-actions#about-billing-for-github-actions)

While most projects won't come close to either of these limits there are likely to still be a reasonable number whose needs would fall in between. 

It seems like most of the current actions and examples are built to use the MacOS runner but other than the few that are for explicitly testing on a Mac most could also be configured to run on a Linux runner. While it seems like a pain, this is a significant enough cost difference that it seems to justify favoring the latter whenever possible.

title: Work around images now having R installed by default
description:
https://github.com/actions/virtual-environments/issues/1220 installs R by default on the GitHub Action images. Unfortunately this version of R is quite old (at least on linux) and on macOS uses the homebrew version of R rather than the CRAN cask.

The `setup-r` action currently does not install R if an existing version of R is on the `PATH`, to allow you to use custom containers with the action.

We will have to remove this feature and provide some other way to avoid installing R if needed.

To resolve to R 4.0 on linux, windows, or macos

title: Broken links to system libraries with Rstudio package manager libraries
description:
**Describe the bug**
I've been encountering library loading errors using the [standard-ci workflow](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/master/examples#standard-ci-workflow) such as:
```
##[error]Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘stringi’ in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...):
 unable to load shared object '/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/stringi/libs/stringi.so':
  libicui18n.so.55: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
I believe this is stemming from the use of the RSPM environment variable (RStudio Package Manager) `'devel', rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/focal/latest"` which installs binaries even when installing from source is explicitly requested. 

 In brief, the workflow command `install.packages("stringi", type="source", configure.args="--disable-icu-bundle")` surprisingly leads to `installing *binary* package ‘stringi’ ...` Full logs below

**To Reproduce**
https://github.com/DSSG-eiCompare/actions-playground/runs/949728389?check_suite_focus=true

**Expected behavior**
There are two issues here really. 1) Something is going on with the binary builds from RPSM unsuccessfully linking to system libraries. And 2) I expect running `install.packages("stringi", type="source")` in a workflow will install from source or raise an error if no source distribution exists in the repository. 

**Additional context**
Current workarounds:
1) Comment the RPSM environment variable and the workflow succeeds, pulling the source from `https://cloud.r-project.org`. https://github.com/DSSG-eiCompare/actions-playground/runs/949751654?check_suite_focus=true 

2) Explicitly setting the repository in `install.packages` overrides RPSM: install.packages("stringi", type="source", repos="https://cran.rstudio.com") https://github.com/DSSG-eiCompare/actions-playground/runs/949768573?check_suite_focus=true

```sh

  shell: /bin/bash -e {0}

title: Caching and precompiled binaries
description:
Hi, thanks for your work on this project! It's cool stuff.

I'm working on a data science workflow with GitHub Actions. I have an `renv.lock` file with all my package dependencies, and I have been recently using the RPackageManager precompiled binaries to quickly install dependencies on the GitHub Actions runners.

I tried using the `renv` cache approach from the Blogdown example, and I'm noticing that there's not much speed difference between [runs where I use the cache](https://github.com/elleobrien/env_exp/runs/1334832081?check_suite_focus=true) and [runs when I don't](https://github.com/elleobrien/env_exp/runs/1334827002?check_suite_focus=true). Looking at the logs, it looks like even though I have the cache, the precompiled binaries are still getting downloaded and installed- for example....

```Installing pillar [1.4.6] ...
	OK [installed binary]
Installing pkgconfig [2.0.3] ...
	OK [installed binary]
Installing tibble [3.0.4] ...
	OK [installed binary]
Installing ggplot2 [3.3.2] ...
	OK [installed binary]
Installing palmerpenguins [0.1.0] ...
	OK [installed binary]
```
So my question is-

does caching make any sense for precompiled binary R packages? Or am I doing this wrong?

title: Setup R devel based on its version
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Running a GitHub action where `r-lib/actions/setup-r@master` contains an unreleased (devel) R version runs the latest stable R version instead of R devel.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow to setup R devel by indicating its respective R version. Currently, R devel is 4.1.0 so this should work:

```
- uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@master
        with:
          r-version: 4.1.0
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is for the user to understand that 4.1.0 corresponds to an unreleased R version and to use `r-version: devel` (not sure yet how to do this automatically).

title: Documentation: specify name for each action example in the examples README
description:
Not a bug but not really a feature request either. A suggested improvement to the [`actions/examples` README](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/master/examples), to make things a little clearer for newcomers using `usethis::use_github_action()`.

## Outline of the issue

The text of the README doesn't actually specify what to pass as the `name` parameter of `usethis::use_github_action()` for each option. It's not hard to find out, or to guess, but I think the documentation would be better if this information were explicitly included.

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65686873/github-action-failing-with-r-cmd-check-using-old-commit

https://github.com/Azure/Microsoft365R/runs/1688860494?check_suite_focus=true

title: Control what rtools folders are added to PATH
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
By default when rtools in installed on Windows, an environment variable `RTOOLS40_HOME` (for the latest version) is created.
To enable R builds, `PATH` should be modified to include *only* `${RTOOLS40_HOME}\usr\bin` (see https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/), which contains `make`.
In contrast, `setup-r@v1` adds *two* paths, the other one being `${RTOOLS40_HOME}\mingw64\bin`, as can be seen from this code snippet (if I understand everything correctly)
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/b53babd4c8bdd1346bcfe6abda6e24fb0863134d/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L320-L325

This extra folder contaminates library search paths and confuses linker in certain scenarios.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Assuming there are CIs that rely on this behavior, this path cannot be removed by default.
However, a boolean switch can be added to control whether this extra folder should be emitted to the system path.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative I am using right now is a complete rewrite of the virtual machine's path, using the following `pwsh` command
```pwsh
$temp = $env:Path -split [System.IO.Path]::PathSeparator | ? {$_ -notlike "*rtools*mingw*"} | join-string -Separator $([System.IO.Path]::PathSeparator)
echo $temp | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8
```

title: select clang compiler on macOS
description:
I included `r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1` in my [`.github/workflows/check-standard.yml`](https://github.com/slowkow/ggrepel/blob/master/.github/workflows/check-standard.yaml) file in ggrepel.

On macOS, the `setup-r` action runs `brew install gcc`

https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/80aabb5e36fe2bd045375760b142ec625140e60c/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L92

Then, during package compilation, the new compiler is used instead of the default macOS clang compiler.

Why is this a problem? For [some C++ code](https://github.com/slowkow/ggrepel/issues/184), we will observe two different behaviors when we try to compile it with different compilers:

1. The default macOS compiler throws an error. This is the one users will use on their machines when they run `install.packages("ggrepel")`. Many users have never installed `brew` and have never run `brew install gcc`.
2. The new compiler installed by `brew install gcc` does not throw an error. This is the one GitHub Actions will use.

Therefore, I believe that we can have an undesirable situation where:
- The code successfully builds on macOS Github Actions.
- The code fails to build on a user's macOS machine.

I may be missing something. Maybe there's something I can add to my ggrepel package that overcomes this issue? I already solved my issue by modifying the C++ code to a version that compiles with the default macOS compiler.

However, I think I would prefer for the build step in GitHub Actions to use the same compiler that my users will use on their own machines.

What do you think? Does this make sense?

Looking forward to learning from you!

title: Having a step that will install dependencies from binary if installing from source fails
description:
**Background**
My understanding is that for new package submissions to CRAN the source is uploaded and the version on CRAN is updated to that source, but the binaries are available within 1 or 2 days **after** the source is uploaded. The exact time will vary by operating system.

**Why does this matter for GitHub Actions (GHA)?**
The default `type` argument for `remotes::install_deps()` to install the package dependencies is `"both"`, which means that the action will use binary if it is available and current, otherwise try installing from source. The problem is that some packages will fail when installed from source when the existing binary on CRAN will install successfully and satisfy the dependency requirement. In short, using `"both"` may cause your build to fail because it's trying hard to get the most recent version of a package even if it's not needed and doesn't know if that source can even be installed successfully versus the binary.

**An example**
On Jul 23, 2020 {XML} v3.99-0.5 was uploaded to CRAN and labeled the most recent source, but the Windows binary was still v3.99-04. {XML} cannot be installed from source on Windows, so the action fails the whole workflow because of the lag between source and binaries being updated on CRAN. when the existing binary would have been fine. Here is my GHA log: https://github.com/StevenMMortimer/salesforcer/runs/904955696?check_suite_focus=true

**Potential Solutions**
The heart of my question is: Should workflows, by default, install only from "binary" for Windows and Mac, rather than "both" to protect against issues like this? Alternatively, developers could specifically include in their workflow which packages to install from binary in a separate call instead of using "both". I'm okay with the latter, but wanted to raise so that people are aware that using "both" (the default) could fail your build when certain packages were recently uploaded to CRAN during the time your GHA workflow is run. A third option would be a fail-safe that's part of `install_deps()` that will try to install from source and if that fails, then try to install from the binary as long as the version meets the dependency requirement.

**Consideration**
I'm not sure I can reliably check what can and cannot be install from source on different operating systems and I'm not sure when another developer will upload a new version of a dependency so the only way to find this type of "issue" is through trial and error. If there's a good way to check, then it's less of an issue, but if not, then I would think the safer option is just to always install as binary when the OS is Windows or Mac unless the `install_deps()` would try both binary and source in the event that source failed.

title: Render Rmarkdown failing when file is renamed or when longer commit history is pushed
description:
The [Render Rmarkdown](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/master/examples#render-rmarkdown) action fails when a file is renamed and when a longer local commit history is pushed. A fix is proposed below.

The issue is that the current Action Workflow only compares the two *latest* commits, rather than comparing the lastest commit on GitHub to the current commit. Furthermore, when a file is renamed, then the current workflow still attempts to render the deleted file.

An example of the file renaming bug can be seen in this repository: [https://github.com/OlivierBinette/rmdActionBug](https://github.com/OlivierBinette/rmdActionBug)

# Fix

1. Change `fetch-depth: 2` to `fetch-depth: 0` to fetch all the commit history
2. Change 
  `RMD_PATH=($(git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r HEAD | grep '[.]Rmd$'))`
to
  `RMD_PATH=($(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | grep '[.]Rmd$'))`
in order to compare the last commit on GitHub to the current commit.
3. Change
  `Rscript -e 'for (file in commandArgs(TRUE)) rmarkdown::render(file)' ${RMD_PATH[*]}`
to
  `Rscript -e 'files=commandArgs(TRUE); files=files[file.exists(files)]; cat("Attempting to render the following files: ", files, "\n"); for (f in files) rmarkdown::render(f)' ${RMD_PATH[*]}`
in order to only render existing files.

title: R-devel macOS: Toolchain changes
description:
Two days ago Simon announced that R4.0 will use gfortran 8.2 and Apples native compiler along with the SDK 10.13.

There is a new alpha R4.0 branch that contains the latest R-devel changes: https://mac.r-project.org/.
There is a need to switch to the new gfortran version and change the URL for getting the R-devel tarball.

The R-devel el-capitan build is stuck at March-25 and might no longer be updated (not 100% sure about this though).

FYI: There are known issues with the 10.15 SDK (Rcpp issues you are most likely aware of, igraph issues). Therefore I am using a custom install of the 10.13 SDK. Maybe you also want to use that as the default SDK on Actions to mimic CRAN behavior?

```sh
wget https://github.com/phracker/MacOSX-SDKs/releases/download/10.15/MacOSX10.13.sdk.tar.xz
tar fxz MacOSX10.13.sdk.tar.xz
sudo mv MacOSX10.13.sdk /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/
rm -rf MacOSX10.13*
```

.R/Makevars

```
CFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX10.13.sdk
CCFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX10.13.sdk
CXXFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX10.13.sdk
CPPFLAGS=-isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX10.13.sdk
```

title: default `R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS` to false on Windows?
description: I believe CRAN sets R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS to false on Windows since some packages are not available for  that OS.  Would it make sense to have this be set automatically in the Windows-based CI checks here as well? title: Rename `Cache R packages` step
description:
It might promote understanding in users of these actions if this name was better aligned with what the step actually does.
