title: Make Ubuntu versions that use_github_actions() functions output more consistent (16.04 vs 20.04)
description:
Running the following reproducible example with the latest dev version of the package outputs this:

```r
usethis::use_github_action_check_full()
file.edit(".github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml") # open the file
```

Relevant part of the output:

```
jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}

    name: ${{ matrix.config.os }} (${{ matrix.config.r }})

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: macOS-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: '3.6'}
          - {os: ubuntu-16.04,   r: 'devel', rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest", http-user-agent: "R/4.0.0 (ubuntu-16.04) R (4.0.0 x86_64-pc-linux-gnu x86_64 linux-gnu) on GitHub Actions" }
          - {os: ubuntu-16.04,   r: 'release', rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest"}
          - {os: ubuntu-16.04,   r: 'oldrel',  rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest"}
          - {os: ubuntu-16.04,   r: '3.5',     rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest"}
          - {os: ubuntu-16.04,   r: '3.4',     rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest"}
          - {os: ubuntu-16.04,   r: '3.3',     rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/xenial/latest"}
```

I would expect the Ubuntu versions to be updated to the latest stable release. This will increase the proportion of checks that pass, especially for packages that have external dependencies. 

Updating the Ubuntu version would also make the package more internally consistent. Adding the 'standard' check yields a version of Ubuntu that was published 4 years later, which is much more useful for developers and less likely to need custom .yml files to add new repos (e.g. as links to this issue show https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/163 )  :

```r
usethis::use_github_action_check_standard()
file.edit(".github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml") # open the file
```

Relevant part of the output:

```
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: macOS-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-20.04, r: 'release', rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/focal/latest"}
          - {os: ubuntu-20.04, r: 'devel', rspm: "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/focal/latest"}
```

There may be advantages of using such an old base OS as Ubuntu 16.04 for some purposes but suspect they are greatly outweighed by the advantages of using a more recent Linux OS for most packages. Flagging here I think it could save a lot of time for the many users who don't use `use_github_action_check_standard()` as the first port of call when setting up CI.

A summary of the Ubuntu version resulting from different `use_github_actions()` functions I've tried:

- `use_github_action_check_full()`: 16.04
- `use_github_action_check_standard()`: 20.04
- `use_tidy_github_actions()`: 16.04

There are various possible solutions to make the OS outputs more consistent, including allowing the user to choose the Ubuntu version with a consistent default (I would suggest 20.04 Long Term release for future proofing) and a simpler solution, updating all functions so they consistently use the latest Long Term Support version of Ubuntu by default. There may be other good solutions and maybe good reasons for the inconsistency highlighted above that I'm not aware of, but confident that making the Ubuntu versions outputed by these CI commands consistent and more up-to-date will save lots of time for `usethis` users.

title: pak should not be cached
description:
**Describe the bug**

In examples workflows using pak, pak's latest version is installed.
However, because the whole library is cached, pak's installation is overwritten by the cached version.

**To Reproduce**
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1572 where I needed pak to use a DESCRIPTION field called "Config/Needs/website". I use it twice, once before the cache step, one after that. The first time things work fine because pak's latest version is installed, the second time there is a failure because pak from the cache is used.

**Expected behavior**
I would expect the workflow to install and use the latest pak version throughout.

**Additional context**

I found https://github.com/actions/toolkit/issues/713 which isn't solved yet, so one cannot exclude pak from the cache path.

Cc @gaborcsardi @hadley

title: Incorrect Rtools installation behavior when another installation already exists in the default place
description:
**Describe the bug**
The `setup-r` action installs R and Rtools on Windows. 
Due to a number of reasons, it is possible that there already exists an installation of Rtools at the default path (`C:\rtools40` for R4.x).
With the recent release of [`Rtools40v2`](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/), a possible bug has surfaced.
If a system image ships with a pre-installed version of Rtools40 found at the default location, the `setup-r` action will not install a newer version of Rtools40v2 even if asked explicitly using `rtools-version: '40v2'`.
This happens because the action script relies on a very poor rtools version check, using only the first character in the version string to distinguish between Rtools35 (version `"35"`, tested value is `"3"`) and Rtools40 (version `"40"`, tested values is `"4"`).
When the desired version is Rtools40v2 (version `"40v2"`, tested value is again `"4"`), it is indistinguishable from the previous version of Rtools40 (or any other future version of Rtools that has a version string starting with `"4"`).
If at the same time Rtools40 is present at the default path, no action is taken and the CI is set up with an older version of Rtools.

This issues potentially blocks migration to the Rtools40v2 (see https://github.com/r-lib/actions/pull/287), because even if the correct version is supplied, no action will be taken if an older version is already present in the system.

**To Reproduce**
To reproduce one needs a CI scenario that relies on the new features added in 40v2 that are absent in 40.
As part of investigating the 40v2, I ran some CI examples (to be honest, a lot before I realised why it is not working).
To be able to debug the `setup-r` action, I forked this repo and added simple `core.info()` calls where `core.debug()` are present in the original code, see for example:
https://github.com/Ilia-Kosenkov/actions/commit/c267817c2cf36a9e069044d769bae6b1792135ec

The important line here is the one that prints "Skipping rtools installation", as it is a sign of `setup-r` finding an existing installation of the correct (at least according to current logic) version.
The relevant fragment in this repo is here:
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/0d6c4b3efe82090bc03e99c585d9e89003117931/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L337-L350

Here is an example CI output that request `rtools-version: '40v2'`:
https://github.com/Ilia-Kosenkov/rextendr/runs/2501639308?check_suite_focus=true#step:2:18
Notice how it outputs desired version of `40v2` yet skips installation because it belives the correct version is already there.

However, here is another example where the downloading and installation do happen:
https://github.com/Ilia-Kosenkov/rextendr/runs/2501698409?check_suite_focus=true#step:3:18

This works because prior to installing R I manually purge system's rtools folder (if present), using e.g. a pwsh script
```pwsh
rm C:\rtools40 -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

**Expected behavior**
I do not know if there is a way to determine the version of Rtools and differentiate between Rtools40 and Rtools40v2.
If it is very difficult (or impossible), I'd expect that if I provide an explicit version, the script will install a fresh version of Rtools even if a previously installed version exists. 
It may do so by installing it to another folder and then setting up an env variable like `RTOOLS40_HOME`.

Alternatively, a new script parameter can be added that will force re-installation of R and/or Rtools if set to `true`.

title: Error in lint workflow
description:

![Screenshot from 2021-06-12 16-24-08](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20923812/121774295-5288d280-cb9b-11eb-97a7-b15951b7a290.png)

See the attached log file.

The same error also shows when running the test-coverage, check-release and check-standard workflows. The error is in the "Query Dependencies" step.

I was able to fix the error by replacing the commands:

```
install.packages('remotes') and
install.packages(c("remotes"))
```
with

```
install.packages('remotes', repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org") and

```

In the lint workflow file. Adding the CRAN mirror as a repo fixed the problem. This fix was suggested on this [question on Stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55244209/error-in-contrib-urlrepos-source-in-r-trying-to-use-cran-without-setting-a).

title: Use default-branch macro instead of explicitly naming common default branches
description:
While many projects use either `master` or `main` for default branches, GitHub Actions now has support for arbitrary alternatives with a `$default-branch` macro:

https://github.blog/changelog/2020-07-22-github-actions-better-support-for-alternative-default-branch-names/

I'm making these changes for myself and will happily contribute back once they're tested.

title: Aliases for legacy R versions
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Tidyverse (and Shiny related packages) like to support the latest **four** R versions.  However, there are only aliases for the latest **two** R versions. 

I would enjoy having aliases for the latest **four** R versions. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I'd like two more aliases:
* `old2release`: Release before `oldrelease`. Ex: `oldrelease = "3.6"`, `old2release = "3.5"`
* `old3release`: Release before `old2release`. Ex: `oldrelease = "3.6"`, `old3release = "3.4"`

(Or any standardized alias names that cover these two situations like `veryoldrelease` and `superoldrelease`)

By having aliases for all _supported_ R versions, it will always be a sliding window and I will not have to manually update the values across _all_ packages that I maintain.

In https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/26, you described how you now hash the major and minor version being installed (https://github.com/r-lib/actions/commit/c2687dac11bca64e304f295084aa58050d90811d), so caching problems do not seem like an issue anymore.


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* Manually providing the numbers. 
	* But this requires manual updates anytime there is a minor R change, which I'd like to avoid in the first place.

title: Remove static R versions from templates: Better default for `http-user-agent` for R devel
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
From #316, the `http-user-agent` is used to help return binary packages from RSPM. 

Most of the GHA workflow templates have a manually defined user agent R version when R is `devel`. It would be great if the workflow templates did not mention a specific R version at all.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
With #325 providing "No static R version", it would be great to have this manually supplied value be the default value when the R version is `devel`. This would also avoid [constant maintenance](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/commit/a880f739a14aad0d50888cb746c1bc2db2257257).

I believe https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/61a5873d25b364d7313bff8c6da063fa43f1777e/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L423-L427 could be updated to include this logic.

title: Have raw R version job names while leveraging alias R versions
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
#330 will allow for static workflow files even if the R version changes. Awesome!

However, the R alias is resolved too late to be used in the matrix job's name. Currently, the titles are not explicit. Ex:

![Screen Shot 2021-07-08 at 11 31 03 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93231/124949997-09803e80-dfe0-11eb-99ef-b70dcfb9c841.png)
Link: https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci-apps/actions/runs/1009577238


**Describe the solution you'd like**
I believe this could be improved on as it is nice to know it is running on R 4.1.... not necessarily `release`.

I've implemented a proof of concept that has an init job (`R Versions`; ~10 seconds) that converts R version aliases into raw R versions and exports them as outputs. These raw values can be used within the R matrix declaration like normal.

![Screen Shot 2021-07-08 at 11 33 38 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/93231/124950799-bd81c980-dfe0-11eb-9e97-e4b65371d329.png)

Code: 
https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci-apps/pull/160/files#diff-7f51f7d2cf1dcaf0944a9fc76e239e3e3dbc018d313c7deff7484459bcab8d2f

If this is something to consider, I propose that the alias conversion steps be consolidated into a single `r-lib/actions` step that exports 5 variables which can be reexported by the job.  This would clean up the `R Versions` init job into something that could be shared with everyone.

Should I add the `R Versions` init job into #330?

**Additional context**
I do not believe this adds extra API calls to convert the alias R versions into raw R versions. Instead of performing the call at run time, all values are called when initialized.

title: Feature request: a reverse dependency check action
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Running reverse dependency checks is time consuming, compute intensive and requires a lot of local installs that take disk space.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A GitHub Action that runs the reverse dependency check. Since revdepchecking is quite expensive, it should not happen on every push. I suggest to do a filter based on branch name or commit message, e.g. branch name matching regex `^revdepcheck.*$` or commit message containing `run revdepcheck`.

I am not sure the GitHub Action time limit is getting in our way here.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* Running the process manually locally with the problems described above.
* running `revdepcheck::cloud_check()` results in 
```r
#> Error: Cloud error (403): Forbidden
#> Message: Forbidden
```

Because according to the [vignette](https://r-lib.github.io/revdepcheck/articles/cloud.html), non-RStudio people don't have access to this.

**Additional context**

title: Render README always results in conflict for pull requests
description:
**Describe the bug**
I am using the GitHub Action template to render my README.Rmd to README.md. However, whenever I open a pull request (e.g. from dev to main branch), I have a conflict of the README.md and a figure that gets created during the rendering

**To Reproduce**
Here is my workflow file: 
```
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - development
    paths:
      - README.Rmd

name: Render-README

jobs:
  render:
    name: Render README
    runs-on: macOS-latest
    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v1
      - name: Install rmarkdown, remotes, and the local package
        run: |
          install.packages("remotes")
          remotes::install_local(".")
          remotes::install_cran("rmarkdown")
          remotes::install_cran("covr")
        shell: Rscript {0}
      - name: Render README
        run: Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("README.Rmd")'
      - name: Commit results
        run: |
          git config --local user.email "actions@github.com"
          git config --local user.name "GitHub Actions"
          git add README.md man/figures/README-*
          git commit -m 'Re-build README.Rmd' || echo "No changes to commit"
          git push origin || echo "No changes to commit"
```

**Conflicting files**
```
README.md
man/figures/README-plot-1.png
```

**Additional context**
The GitHub action itself works without problems

title: Allow `setup-r-dependencies` to accept `working-directory` or similar functionality
description:
I am in the process of moving my package's, [L0Learn](https://github.com/hazimehh/L0Learn), CI/CD to GitHub Actions. Currently, I am facing an issue where `setup-r-dependencies` fails because the R package is in a sub-directory of my repo.

The cause of this issue is found here as the directory that `pak` inspects for dependencies is hardcoded as `local::.`:
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/fd9a09a778173fe57e2801815a36d73473f8bba7/setup-r-dependencies/action.yaml#L24

I am rather new to using Github Actions, so I am unsure of which of these solutions (if any) would be better:
- Make`setup-r-dependencies` action aware of the `working-directory` parameter in the greater "workflow action scope" 
- Create a new input parameter for subdirectories similar to how `install_github` from devtools(https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/devtools/versions/1.13.6/topics/install_github)

```bash
Error: Error: <callr_remote_error: Cannot install packages:
  * local::.: No root directory found in /Users/runner/work/L0Learn/L0Learn or its parent directories. Root criterion: contains a file "DESCRIPTION" with contents matching "^Package: ">
   in process 20845 
  -->
  <simpleError: Cannot install packages:
  * local::.: No root directory found in /Users/runner/work/L0Learn/L0Learn or its parent directories. Root criterion: contains a file "DESCRIPTION" with contents matching "^Package: ">
```

I would be happy to submit a PR for this change, if this new functionality is deemed valuable.
Meanwhile, are there any workarounds for this issue?

title: Should the DESCRIPTION be more real?
description:
I was analyzing a bunch of "our" repos, looking at various aspects of the DESCRIPTION file, for some usethis work. I was looking at different ways to detect something is "ours".

The two main ways to tell this from DESCRIPTION:

1. Having a GitHub URL which reveals the source repo is owned by one of our GitHub orgs (tidyverse, r-lib, tidymodels)
2. Having RStudio listed as a funder among the authors

I suspect it would make sense for the DESCRIPTION file here to be a bit more real, even though I realize this is not an R package. DESCRIPTION remains a really useful source of metadata for us.

title: Format examples as reusable workflows
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Typically I have copy/pasted workflows from the examples into many different R repositories. However, this means I have no clue which version I am using, and requires making changes to many files when workflows run into errors.

In addition, nearly every person using github actions on an R package has done something similar (because these examples are great!)

**Describe the solution you'd like**
[Reusable workflows](https://github.blog/changelog/2021-10-05-github-actions-dry-your-github-actions-configuration-by-reusing-workflows/) are now in public beta, and it would be great to reference the examples directly from the r-lib/actions  repository. For instance, it would be possible to just reference the reusable workflow from the main branch, so any updates to the examples would be added; if someone didn't want updates, however, they could use a more specific reference, such as a tag or commit.

I think this would be simple to implement by  adding `workflow_call:` to `on:` within the yaml files:

```
on: 
  workflow_call:
```


**Describe alternatives you've considered**
I know `usethis` can be helpful, but it would require manually updating workflows and essentially copy/pasted code.

**Additional context**

title: Ensure `crayon.enabled` has one of the supported values
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
`crayon.enabled` is a parameter
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/fd9a09a778173fe57e2801815a36d73473f8bba7/setup-r/action.yml#L15-L17

It is written to the `options()` in `.Rprofile`
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/fd9a09a778173fe57e2801815a36d73473f8bba7/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L485-L501

The default value is `NULL`, which seems to translate to the empty string in the string interpolation fragment above.
As a result, in a rare case `.Rprofile` can get the following contents
```R
options(
# ...
crayon.enabled =, #notice the absence of value, this is invalid syntax in R
#...
)
```
As a result, any step that relies on `Rscript` execution fails with an invalid syntax error.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
According to docs, `crayon.enabled` is a `logical` scalar. Therefore it should be set to either `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `NULL` (as in R literal, not `ts` string), with `NULL` indicating *not-set* value.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Updating workflows to ensure `crayon.enabled` is set explicitly.
Cloning/forking the repository and modifying the actions script.

**Additional context**
This issue may arise only in some edge cases, still, I believe the arguments should be type-safe, and their values should be validated before writing any script/configuration file.

title: setup-r-dependencies fails on debian docker image
description:
`setup-r-dependencies` fails on debian docker images such as `rocker/r-base` (or its derivatives). It is because `pak:: pkg_system_requirements ` [does not support debian](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/15b0b2e9d5d81d3853627a69edcb6d2118a6e36c/R/system-requirements.R).

I understand that `setup-r-dependencies` is designed only to work with github runner systems but not docker images. It would still be nice to have a setting to make running `pak:: pkg_system_requirements` optional as the system requirements are often come with the docker image (or user can easilly install them via `apt-get`).

title: Setting new options in R profile at R setup
description:
I would like to be able to setup some R options for a workflow. For example 
```
options(tinytex.verbose = TRUE)
```

I could do that at the step where I need it, but it seems kind of the same type of options than `crayon.enabled` defined in the .Rprofile. 
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/b75d3e0c21718c20529373a7dd35ff5e1c1a5759/setup-r/src/installer.ts#L360-L368
It would be easier to be able to setup some R options to put in the .Rprofile for a whole workflow just after R installation. 

I don't know what could be done for passing those option in `setup-r` but maybe some field can be added to be used in `with:` to be written with the above options. 

Currently, I am doing this 
```yaml
      - name: Add some R options for later steps
        run: cat("\noptions(tinytex.verbose = TRUE)\n", file = "~/.Rprofile", append = TRUE)
        shell: Rscript {0}
```
This is also fine. However, I suppose you are already setting option in user's Rprofile too.
Having the ability to set those in a `with:` field under setup R would save a step and insure the same Rprofile file is used. 

A more flexible solution could also be to add the Rprofile path as output of `setup-r` so that one can easily append to it. or `setup-r` could set the env var `R_PROFILE_USER` to a standard path to use on each OS and for other step to use it. 

Nothing blocking here, just an idea if you think it worths it.

title: Possible breaking changes to `macos-latest` runner for older versions of R
description:
Hi folks,

I've noticed some builds starting to fail that were previously fine, and I think it may be due to a breaking change being rolled out to the `macos-latest` image. The image is being upgraded to Big Sur starting from September 15th, with the migration intending to be completed by November 3rd. See the [relevant issue](https://github.com/actions/virtual-environments/issues/4060), which notes that "R was not available for Big Sur when we prepared the image for the first time."

We can force a particular OS with `macos-10.15` or `macos-11`. Here's a summary of success/failure with build links:

* [Successful build for R 4.0.5 on `macos-10.15`](https://github.com/mdneuzerling/parity/runs/3916617126?check_suite_focus=true)
* [Failing build for R 3.6.3 on `macos-11`](https://github.com/mdneuzerling/parity/runs/3916591701?check_suite_focus=true)
* [Failing build for R 4.0.5 on `macos-11`](https://github.com/mdneuzerling/parity/runs/3916596356?check_suite_focus=true)
* [Successful build for R 4.1.1 on `macos-11`](https://github.com/mdneuzerling/parity/runs/3916605795?check_suite_focus=true)

The job I've got is very simple, and doesn't depend on repository contents. It simply sets up R and runs `Rscript -e '1+1'`.

```yaml
jobs:
  failing-big-sur-reprex:
    runs-on: macos-11

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up R 4.0.5
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1
        with:
          r-version: '4.0.5'

      - name: Verify Rscript exists
        run: |
          Rscript -e '1+1'
```

title: Prevent installing the package itself in setup-r-dependencies
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When installing package dependencies, it might be desirable / convenient not to install the package itself, which is also the approach of e.g. [`pak::local_install_dev_deps()`](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/local_package_trees.html#details). Action `setup-r-dependencies` however does install the package.

- A use-case we have is a package that needs to be checked (and installed) headlessly.
- For a CI workflow running `R CMD check`, the installation is unneccessary and might waste some precious time (e.g. with compiled code).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Allow not installing the package itself in `setup-r-dependencies`, driven e.g. by a new "parameter" under `with:`.
- Consider whether not installing the package might be the sensible default behavior (given `R CMD check` considerations from above).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The alternative is to not use `setup-r-dependencies` and go for the old, lengthy approach taking explicit care of caching in the workflows, like in the pre-`setup-r-dependencies` examples, e.g. https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/a880f739a14aad0d50888cb746c1bc2db2257257/examples/check-standard.yaml

**Additional context**
`NULL`

title: setup-r-dependencies: caches for R-devel become invalid every next day
description:
The restore key for caches in `setup-r-dependencies` uses `R.Version()$version.string`. 

For, R-devel, it is something like
```
[1] "R Under development (unstable) (2021-11-08 r81154)"
```
Therefore, the cache becomes invalid once a new version of R-devel is pushed. I am not sure if it is intended though.  The original method of using
```
> sprintf("R-%i.%i", getRversion()$major, getRversion()$minor)
[1] "R-4.2"
```
works better for R-devel and preserves the cache for longer period of time.

title: Allow failure for `setup-r-dependencies@v1`?
description:
**Describe the bug**
In `setup-r-dependencies@v1`, if installation of a dependency fails, the GHA stops with an error, thus skipping all unit tests. It should be an option to allow dependency installation failure.

For example, if your package A only depends on R >= 3.4 but contains some S3 extensions of package B, you would have unit tests for package A (which has package B in `Suggests`) that (1) check functionality on R 3.4 and (2) check functionality of the S3 extension of package B. This is currently not possible if package B is dependent on e.g., R 3.5. In the GitHub Action for R 3.4, installation of package B will fail since it requires R 3.5:

```

  * ggtext: Needs R 3.5 
```

title: Action to update testthat snapshots
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Updating testthat snapshots is often forgotten. With snapshot variants in testthat >= 3.1.1, this also becomes tedious, because it may be difficult to replicate the conditions under which a variant is activated.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I have implemented a composite action in https://github.com/cynkra/dm/tree/main/.github/workflows/update-snapshots and elsewhere. Should it live here?

Snapshots are run for the test files that contain the string `"snapshot"`, changes to `tests/testthat/_snaps` are sent as a pull request against the head branch with an unambiguous branch name determined from the matrix condig. Works for both pushes and pull request. In case of changes, the action aborts the job, because subsequent checks are then based on a weird state of the code.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Committing to the head branch directly may lead to surprises and race conditions, I think pull requests are better here.

title: setup-r: use more stable macOS binary URLs
description:
The macOS build URLs currently used for R installation are inherently unstable, because a release package is only present if the nightly build succeeded. In cases when the nightly build did not succeed (like last night) the `setup-r` action will fail.

There are now URLs that contain the latest _successful_ build binaries and will not be deleted on failure. They have the form:

    https://mac.R-project.org/<oscode>/last-success/<R-flavor>-<arch>.pkg
    https://mac.R-project.org/<oscode>/last-success/<R-flavor>-<arch>.tar.xz

The latter is just the `R.framework` part of the package for convenience and faster installation - the content is identical to the release package.

So, for example, to install `R-devel` framework from the `high-sierra` build a suggested equivalent action would be:

    curl -L https://mac.R-project.org/high-sierra/last-success/R-devel-x86_64.tar.xz | \
      sudo tar fxj - -C /Library/Frameworks

This is should be stable even if nightly builds fail.

title: render-rmarkdown: Does not find files to commit
description:
**Describe the bug**
render-rmarkdown: Files do not seem to be found using the given YAML when trying to commit.

I have a very simple repo, with a README.Rmd at the root, which outputs a github_document, which means rendering a markdown .md file. When pushing with the YAML given in the example, the action passes, but nothing appears to be committed (i.e. no changes on the displayed .md at the repo root) on github. 

This line is where those changes should be committed:
`git commit ${RMD_PATH[*]/.Rmd/.md} -m 'Re-build Rmarkdown files' || echo "No changes to commit"`

but there is no commit and instead the text "No changes to commit" is shown in the logs. However, the files clearly are being found earlier on, when we render the rmarkdowns, as this can be seen in the logs. 

I can fix the issue by adding a `git add *[.Rmd/.md]` on the line above. However, I assume this shouldn't be necessary as it would expect to work out the box.

I will admit that I have made minor changes to the YAML file, as it did not work out the box originally. For example, curl couldn't be found/installed when doing setup-renv and so that step was removed and replaced with a setup-r-dependencies with extra-packages as curl and rmarkdown under what I believe to be the advice given [here](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/416).

Link to action and logs:

https://github.com/MangoTheCat/bambooHR/runs/4922660409?check_suite_focus=true

title: documentation: use of `Rscript()` on Windows
description:
I notice that the default style in this repo for using `Rscript()` seems to be something like:

```yaml
      - name: Build site
        run: Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site_github_pages(new_process = FALSE, install = FALSE)'
```

I found out (after much fun), that this won't work the way you expect on Windows:

```yaml
      - name: Say hello
        run: Rscript -e 'print("hello")'
```

Windows parses this as `hello`, rather than `"hello"`. However, This *does* work on Windows:

```yaml
      - name: Say hello
        run: Rscript -e "print('hello')"
```

I found a good writeup on this here:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62954030/rscript-behaves-inconsistently-on-windows-with-single-and-double-quotes

I had a quick look here, and none of the actions in ths repo suffer from this (you would have noticed already).

I would be happy to make a PR add a few words somewhere, but I would have to rely on you to suggest a place.

Thanks!

If you run into this stringi loading error on Ubuntu, it is because the RSPM stringi package needs a rebuild. We notified the RSPM team. Subscribe to this issue if you want to hear about the resolution.

A temporary workaround is to recompile stringi. Add this after the `setup-r-dependencies` step:

```yaml
      - name: stringi workaround on Linux
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'     
        run: install.packages("stringi", repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com")
        shell: Rscript {0}

```

title: Test an R package against e.g. a Julia package on github actions
description:
This is maybe less of a feature request than a question, so please close this issue if this is the wrong place to ask (but it might be a great feature for my use case 😃): 

Is it possible to test an R package against a Julia package using github actions? 

Suppose I added a package that links R and Julia to suggests, e.g. JuliaCall or JuliaConnectoR, and included both Julia and the Julia package as a SystemRequirement. Would github actions be able to install the R package, Julia, the Julia package, and be 'smart enough' to link Julia and R? 

To connect Julia and R via JuliaCall or JuliaConnectoR, there is some additional overhead - for JuliaConnectoR to find Julia, one has to add Julia's installation path to one's local .renviron file, and JuliaCall requires to specify Julia's path via the `julia_setup()` function.

title: Allow disabling cache in `setup-r-dependencies`
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'm trying to use [`act`](https://github.com/nektos/act/) to test workflows locally and avoid spamming commits when I'm developing a complex workflow. Unfortunately, it looks like [`act` doesn't support caching](https://github.com/nektos/act/issues/989) and fails whenever caching is included in a step.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like to have a way to disable the cache in `setup-r-dependencies`. Then, it would be possible for `act` users to do:

```yml
- uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
  with:
    cache: ${{ !env.ACT }}
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I can't think of any other good alternative. The only option would be to go way to the 'old' way of manually installing dependencies (with remotes) but it means losing all the benefit brought by `setup-r-dependencies`.

title: Run apt-get update before apt-get install
description:
**Describe the bug**

System dependency install sometimes fails

**To Reproduce**

https://github.com/r-hub/cransays/runs/6240547671?check_suite_focus=true

(It was not a one off failure. Hourly Builds have consistently failed during >12h. Build `#1821` to `#1836` here: https://github.com/r-hub/cransays/actions/workflows/render-dashboard.yml).

**Expected behavior**

Attempt to fetch the package to install fails with a 404 because `apt` is attempting to fetch an outdated version that has been removed from the repos. Instead, it should fetch & install the current version, which it can know by running `apt update` before running `apt install`.

I confirmed that adding `apt update` solves the issue in this build: https://github.com/r-hub/cransays/actions/runs/2250367839.

**Additional context**

My specific use case is with `install-r-dependencies` but this should also affect any action which runs `apt-get install`.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am trying to force an action to only install binaries of dependencies (i.e., not build from source when the source version is later than the binary and the package requires compilation). [setting the environment variable here](https://github.com/bcgov/bcmaps/runs/7926254356?check_suite_focus=true#step:5:9) vs [failing on a source install here](https://github.com/bcgov/bcmaps/runs/7926254356?check_suite_focus=true#step:5:441).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Installation during `setup-r-dependencies` action to respect the `R_COMPILE_AND_INSTALL_PACKAGES` environment variable.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
In the past I have created my own step to install dependencies using `install.packages()`, but the `setup-r-dependencies` is very convenient!

**Additional context**
This is very likely more of an issue for `{pak}`, asking for it to respect this env var, but since the instructions here suggest setting it, I thought I would raise it to flag the inconsistent behaviour.

title: Notes on a `noSuggests`-like workflow
description:
Example workflow for yardstick:
https://github.com/tidymodels/yardstick/pull/281/files

A few notes:
- Running with `cache: false` to avoid accidentally restoring Suggested dependencies from a pre-existing cache. Using RSPM means this isn't that painful. We could also use the cache and somehow trim down the resulting library of packages to only what is in the pak lockfile. 
- Only running on Linux with r-release (because of `cache: false`)
- Sets `dependencies: '"hard"'` to install Depends, Imports, LinkingTo dependencies, but not Suggests. Suggests dependencies can still be implicitly installed if they are required by any of the hard dependencies.
- Always installs testthat, knitr, and rmarkdown to be able to run tests and build vignettes. We know the `noSuggests` build installs testthat, but I imagine it also installs knitr/rmarkdown too.

title: Make R 4.1 on Windows a new "special" in `examples/check-full.yaml`
description:
Capturing a recent slack discussion.

We should add R 4.1 + `windows-latest` to the standard matrix in [`examples/check-full.yaml`](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/v2-branch/examples/check-full.yaml).

The argument is similar to that for keeping R 3.6 + `windows-latest` around: making sure to test with a previous toolchain, Rtools35.

With the release of R 4.2, now it's important to test on R 4.1 + `windows-latest` to retain coverage of RTools40 and a native encoding that's not UTF-8.

For practical reasons, this means we will probably drop R 3.6 + `windows-latest` from our standard matrix, since we're already flirting with various limits. Specific packages could choose to retain R 3.6 + `windows-latest` in the matrix, if it has proven to be helpful in recent memory.

We support R release + 4 previous versions on Windows, macOS, and Linux. But we don't test that complete matrix, rather we test one complete row and one complete column in the table below PLUS we add any special high-risk combinations (e.g. R 4.1 + `windows-latest`).

```
           lin win mac
devel      +    -   -
release    +    +   +
oldrel-1   +    -   -
oldrel-2   +    -   -
oldrel-3   +    -   -
oldrel-4   +    -   -
```

title: Confusing and inaccurate documentation of check-r-package inputs
description:
The documentation for the first four inputs for the _check-r-package_ action—`args`, `build_args`, `check-dir`, and `error-on`—each include the statement "It must be an R expression in single quotes."  This is both vague and not entirely true.

Presumably "it" here refers to the sequence characters in the YAML document following the key corresponding to an input and the following `: `.  But what really matters here is not that this sequence be a single-quoted string but that it be a YAML representation of a string corresponding to the desired R expression.  And there are ways to make such a YAML representation that don't involve wrapping the R expression in single quotes.

To give one example, the second example in the action documentation uses the key-value pair `error-on: '"error"'` to set the value of the `error-on` input.  The reason two sets of quotes are needed here is that the double-quote character is an _indicator character_ in YAML (see https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#53-indicator-characters).  If we just write `error-on: "error"`, the YAML parser will see the double-quote characters as YAML string delimiters and will use the value `error` as the value for the key `error-on`, and that will be what it passes on to the application.  Unless the identifier `error` has been assigned a value suitable for `rcmdcheck`'s `error_on` argument (and it almost certainly won't have), the workflow will error out when `rcmdcheck` is called.

That same example uses the key-value pair `args: 'c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")'` to set the value of the `args` input.  In this case, since there is no ambiguity as to what is to be a part of the string and what is merely being used to quote it, the single quotes are completely unnecessary.  We could just as easily have written `args: c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")`.  To YAML, these are simply two different presentations of the same information and the value for `args` passed to the application will be precisely the same in both cases.

Even in the `error-on` case, there are alternatives to using single quotes: for example, we could write `error-on: "\"error\""`.  And since we don't really care what R quoting style we use for the `error_on` argument value, we could also have used `error-on: "'error'"` or even `error-on: '''error'''`.  And since we can use any R expression that evaluates to a suitable value in place of a string literal, we could also use `error-on: c("error")` or even, somewhat perversely, `error-on: paste0("err", "on")`.

All this would be somewhat academic if all you ever wanted to do was pass string literals and character vectors in as the values for the action inputs.  In this case, the advice "It must be an R expression in single quotes." is serviceable enough, even if somewhat misleading and not quite true.  Where it starts to matter is in the case where you want to use Workflow expressions instead of string literals for the action input values.

Suppose, for example, you want to allow the user to specify the value for the `error_on` argument as an input to a `workflow_dispatch` event.  The "on" section of the workflow might look like this:
```
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      error-on:
        description: 'Value for error-on'
        type: string
        default: '"error"'
```

and the _check_ step of the workflow might look like this:
```
- uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
    with:
      args: 'c("--no-manual", "--as-cran")'
      error-on: ${{ github.event.inputs.error-on }}
      check-dir: '"check"'
```

A user might read that the input value "must be an R expression in single quotes" and type `'"error"'` in the text input box.  This would be wrong and cause a workflow error.  What should be typed is `"error"` (or `'error'`).  This clearly shows that the value supplied for the `error-on` key must be the R expression itself; the need for single-quoting that value in certain select cases only arises when YAML cannot otherwise discern unambiguously precisely what that value is.

title: Rtools 42 adds MinGW to the path
description:
It seems that when installing rtools 42 the mingw compiler is added to the `PATH` even if setting the `windows-path-include-mingw` variable. This contradicts what's documented [here](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/v2-branch/setup-r/action.yml#L35):

> This argument is now defunct on Rtools40 and later, which never add the mingw directory to the path.

I wonder if we could re-add support for that flag for rtools 42. In my use case, having mingw in the path causes problems when compiling other libraries.

Here's a link showing that mingw is in the PATH: https://github.com/dfalbel/testrtools/runs/6798819503?check_suite_focus=true#step:4:12

FWIW the Rtools42 [documentation](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools42/rtools.html) states that one of the differences compared to rtools40 is that R adds the compiler toolchain to the PATH (??) when installed:

> When R is installed from the binary installer, PATH to the compiler toolchain and build tools is set automatically (by R) based on the default location, information in the registry, or the R_CUSTOM_TOOLS_PATH variable.

title: Test failures in code coverage GHA and how to investigate them further
description:
I am using the [example](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/v2-branch/examples/test-coverage.yaml) code-coverage GHA across multiple respos, and I am often seeing tests fail while computing coverage when they don't fail otherwise.

For example,  even though none of the tests fail in [R CMD Check](https://github.com/easystats/bayestestR/runs/5866705259?check_suite_focus=true), some tests seem to [fail](https://github.com/easystats/bayestestR/runs/5866705258?check_suite_focus=true) while computing code coverage.

title: Offering a GitHub Pages-powered deployment instead of Netlify
description:
As Netlify begins to impose service limits, it would be good to provide a template for deploying directly from the action onto GitHub Pages. Specifically, the [`bookdown` action's deployment](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/689e4b260054da2c50e3612b982fec67f30772e0/examples/bookdown.yaml#L50-L57) and [`blogdown` action's deployment](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/689e4b260054da2c50e3612b982fec67f30772e0/examples/blogdown.yaml#L48-L55) emphasizes a Netlify powered site. However, the hard work in building the artifacts deployed is really being done on the GitHub Action runner. The move over to Netlify at this point seems unneeded. So, I'm suggesting a second template be added that focuses on deployment to GitHub Pages. 


In the next part, I sketch out a possible solution I'm currently using. Note, as both of the templates use `macOS-latest` instead of `ubuntu-latest`, we need to use [`actions/upload-artifact`](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact) and [`actions/download-artifact`](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) as [`JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action`](https://github.com/JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action/tree/f2d614329bd4473098c8f0bf2a61766a1c400b0d#operating-system-support-) has poor macOS support.

Within the `bookdown` job, remove the netlify deployment and replace it with: 

```yaml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: _book
          path: _book
```

From there, we add a second job that handles the deployment on ubuntu:

```yaml
  deploy:
   runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   needs: build
   steps:
     - name: Checkout repo
       uses: actions/checkout@v2.3.1
     - name: Download artifact
       uses: actions/download-artifact@v2
       with:
         name: _book 
         path: _book 
     - name: Deploy book
       uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@4.1.3
       with:
         token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
         branch: gh-pages
         folder: _book
```


An alternative approach would be to extract [`pkgdown::deploy_from_branch()`](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/blob/5bd377e7cb6d268565018b73e4bb99d2788182ed/R/deploy-site.R#L100-L106), which is used to [deploy a `pkgdown` site](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/689e4b260054da2c50e3612b982fec67f30772e0/examples/pkgdown.yaml#L44-L48), and generalize it further.

title: Provide single step for installing R packages
description:
e.g. 
```
      - name: Cache R packages
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: ${{ env.R_LIBS_USER }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.get-r-version.outputs.version }}-1-

     - name: Install pak
        run: |
          install.packages("pak", repos = "https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/dev/")
        shell: Rscript {0}

      - name: Install system dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          while read -r cmd
          do
            eval sudo $cmd
          done < <(Rscript -e 'writeLines(pak::local_system_requirements("ubuntu", "16.04"))')

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pak::local_install_dev_deps()
        shell: Rscript {0}

      - name: Session info
        run: |
          options(width = 100)
          pkgs <- installed.packages()[, "Package"]
          sessioninfo::session_info(pkgs, include_base = TRUE)
        shell: Rscript {0}
```

Exposing cache key as top-level variable. Would also need to provide some way to get OS info into `local_system_requirements` call, and should possibly consider setting RSPM env var by default?

title: Example workflow to call rsconnect::writeManifest() for a static site and deploy to a branch.
description:
## Problem

My team and I heavily use RStudio Connect, and we love [Git-backed content](https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/user/git-backed/). Thanks to `pkgdown::deploy_to_branch()` and `usethis::use_github_action("pkgdown")`, it is almost trivially easy to continuously deploy a package site on Connect. However, this pattern requires `manifest.json` at the top level, and pkgdown does not currently create a manifest file. Likewise for `bookdown`, `blogdown`, and other R-focused static site generators.

## Proposal

I propose a new example workflow to call rsconnect::writeManifest() for a static site and deploy to a branch intended for RStudio Connect [Git-backed content](https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/user/git-backed/).

## Alternatives

In https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/issues/1611 and https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/1129, I proposed that `pkgdown` and `bookdown` each write their own manifest files when deploying content to branches. However, it has been a month since then, I am not sure if those ideas will gain traction.

title: Set R temp directory to be in Runner temp directory
description:
On windows, short path name (or 8.3 filename) are still used on GHA. This path can cause issue with some tools - specifically we encounter error on windows with LaTeX when rendering from a `tempfile()`

As nothing is done specifically in `setup-r`, R will look at `%TEMP%` which contains a short filename - this has been reported already and it is normal. (https://github.com/actions/virtual-environments/issues/712)

What about setting `TEMPDIR`, `TMP` or `TEMP` to the runner temp directory by default? (`RUNNER_TEMP`, `runner.temp`, `process.env["RUNNER_TEMP"]`). This is already use to place the R user library (`R_LIBS_USER`). This folder has the advantage to not have space on Windows, so no short file name with `~`.

It could also be a parameter to pass to the action to set the R temp dir to a different location
```yaml
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1
        with:
          temp_directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
```

Currently to make the test pass, I set this environment for the step
```yaml
      - name: Check
        env:
          _R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_: false
          TMPDIR: ${{ runner.temp }}
        run: rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(args = c("--no-manual", "--as-cran"), error_on = "warning", check_dir = "check")
        shell: Rscript {0}
```

I could also do it for the job by setting globally using a custom step
```yaml
      - name: change temp dir
        run: echo "TMPDIR=${{ runner.temp }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        shell: bash
```

it seems this variable can't be define in `env:` at the job level, as it is done with `secrets` (no access to `${{ runner.temp }}` there it seems)

Would it be something to consider ?

title: Caching key collision between different ubuntu versions
description:
RSPM serves separate binaries for Ubuntu 16, 18, or 20. However the default caching-key `${{runner.os}}` only distinguishes between windows, mac, or linux. 

https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/7fa7bf9d60cc18d06953c4e56e056dcadcf64b63/.github/workflows/check-full.yaml#L59-L65

As a result, if you are testing on multiple versions of ubuntu, or if you ever upgrade your version of ubuntu, you end up with cached packages for the wrong version of ubuntu. The result are strange dll errors when loading packages like this: https://github.com/r-lib/textshaping/runs/1067671444?check_suite_focus=true

```
* creating vignettes ... ERROR
##[error]--- re-building ‘c_interface.Rmd’ using rmarkdown
##[error]Error: processing vignette 'c_interface.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:
unable to load shared object '/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/stringi/libs/stringi.so':
  libicui18n.so.66: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

The error looks very cryptic, the cause is that R is loading a build of `stringi` that was compiled against another version of ubuntu, and therefore the wrong version of libicu.

I think the only solution is to add `config.matrix.os` to your caching key, when you are using a matrix. Ideally we would simply use the `runs-on` variable as the key, but I don't think GHA exposes that value in the expression syntax.

The command `\style` takes long because styler is generally slow (I am allowed to say it because I wrote most of it -.- haha).

**Solution: use the cache**

As of styler `v1.3.0`, repeated styling is almost instantaneous because of caching (of whole files but also of top-level expressions). If the cache is activated. And I think it's fair to say that in a PR, only a minority of top-level expressions is changed. `{styler}` uses the  `{R.cache}` backend for caching, and the location of the cache can be specified with `R.cache::setCacheRootPath("/path/to/cache")`, best in the same R session we call `styler::style_pkg()`. Then, we'd have to cache that directory to benefit from speed gains.

I think it's a small thing to implement this, but I have no clue about GitHub Actions, so I hope someone else shows interest in making a code contribution.

title: setup-tinytex: Allow setting custom CTAN mirror
description:
I just had an issue where the main CTAN mirror kept throwing errors (due to timeouts) when iteratively installing a lot of LaTeX packages via `tinytex`. Installing {tinytex} with a different CTAN mirror via `tinytex::install_tinytex(TRUE, repository = )` solved the issue.

This had the nice side-effect of speeding up the {tinytex} installation itself a bit, probably due to less load on the mirror when installing the default packages.

Having this option in the action directly, maybe even in the default config so that users are aware of it, could reduce the load on the main mirror a bit.

title: test-coverage fails if an R package was updated recently and its binary hasn't been built yet
description:
install_deps function of remotes package tries to install a binary of the latest version by default on macOS.
There is no binary of the latest version of an R package if the package was updated recently.
install_deps function fails to install a binary of the latest version in this situation because there is no binary of the latest version.
Thus test-coverage fails.
An example is shown below.
https://github.com/ShotaOchi/imagerExtra/runs/1994659316?check_suite_focus=true

I avoided the error by modifying the line shown below
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/09985adfeecefc56d0e0c5eaeeb68a2a19d60041/examples/test-coverage.yaml#L42
like this.
``` remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE, type = "source") ```

I think it is also a good idea to use Linux instead of macOS because install_deps function doesn't try to download binaries on Linux.

description:

This will be eventually fixed in the installer, but to install older versions of R, a workaround would be nice.

title: render rmarkdown example trigger may be too narrowly set?
description:
**Describe the bug**

Changes to a `renv.lock` file, (or changes to the workflow file) should arguably also trigger the workflow, but it does not since it only looks for changes in `.Rmd` files.  This is a relatively easy fix or adjustment, but then the workflow will still fail because the actual render step is also conditioned only to run on those `.Rmd` files listed in the `git diff` results.

**To Reproduce**

Consider an application of this which uses `renv` to manage versions (as implied by the workflow use of `uses` renv).  If the user attempts to fix a failing render due to, say, a missing `renv` entry, the build won't trigger.  

**Expected behavior**
Changes to `renv.lock` (and possibly changes to the workflow file itself) should also trigger rebuilding (probably of all the .Rmd files). 

**Additional context**
 Of course I might be wrong about this, which is why I'm not proposing a PR here, there's probably other edge cases I'm not thinking about.  Certainly it's arguable that other files (e.g. a `.Rprofile`) would technically also count; and obviously in general an Rmd can depend on any arbitrary file (or internet resource external to the repo).  I guess 'cache invalidation' is famously hard for a reason.  I get that 'advanced' users should write their own actions, and I get that the point here is to minimize load on GH-Actions in common cases, but still not sure it wouldn't be better for the example action to just be less clever (render every time?).  But otherwise, I think the updates to `renv.lock` would be in scope here; since the action depends on renv and the resulting behavior may be difficult to debug.

title: MacOS check fails because of bad autoreconf
description:
I'm not sure if this is the right place to ask about this.  My run https://github.com/dmurdoch/rgl/actions/runs/545149657 of `R CMD check` failed on MacOS, because `autoreconf` wasn't correctly set up:  `aclocal` was missing.  Should that have been part of r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1 ?  

The check code detects that `autoreconf` is installed and tries to run it, but it doesn't work.

The problem is fixed by adding this to my workflow file:

```
      - name: Install automake
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install automake
```

but I don't know if that's the best fix.

title: Upgrade cache action
description:
**Additional context**

Some actions provided here use `actions/cache@v2`, that was released on May 2020 (see https://github.com/actions/cache/releases).

Current version is v2.1.6. In the meantime, some improvements were introduced (specially interesting ones related with verbosity and performance), although it is not completely clear to me if that would affect to R-related actions.

I think it could be also interesting to keep an eye on these updates, and maybe explore the adequacy of an upgrade.

Many thanks

title: Add build_args to check-r-package
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I would like to be able to pass something into the `build_args` parameter of `rcmdcheck`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add an input to the composite action to be passed to `rcmdcheck`.

**Additional context**
I have a forked version of the repo, and can put together a pull request. Just would like to know if there is anything in particular I need to do to match the current standards of the repository.

title: Consider varying time zones
description:
Currently I think all of the actions will set the timezone to UTC during setup but I wonder if it would be worthwhile to allow this to vary. I believe some of the Mac cran machines are configured to a different timezone hence why they will often pick up on issues that have not been noticed previously.

Changing the timezone prior to running R CMD check locally (e.g. `TZ=NZ R CMD check --as-cran`) has in the past helped me find subtle date handling mistakes in one of my packages and it would be good if we could have this flexibility out of the box with actions.

title: Document how to add additional repos
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The problem is indicating another repository for installation when using https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/master/setup-r-dependencies.
An example is [trying to install INLA](https://community.rstudio.com/t/correctly-installing-non-cran-dependencies/114649/) on GitHub Actions.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Solution given by @jimhester 

```yaml
env:
```

title: `setup-renv`: not actually caching installed packages?
description:
When using the `setup-renv@v1` action, I noticed that the caching step only generates a cache of around 22 B:
 
![Screen Shot 2021-10-13 at 17 17 29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38256462/137162861-a6f8d181-3664-40c0-a181-4484d9b7eb51.png)

even when quite a few packages are present in the [`renv.lock`](https://github.com/milanmlft/test-renv-caching/blob/master/renv.lock) file.

When running a subsequent action (without changes to `renv.lock`), the GHA successfully restores the cache but then still needs to re-install all the R packages:

![Screen Shot 2021-10-13 at 17 20 13](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/38256462/137163370-30650ee8-967f-4bf3-b25d-65ec2279a26a.png)

this step always takes approximately the same amount of time, even when there were no changes to `renv.lock`.

So it seems that the caching step in `setup-renv` does not actually cache the R packages and it's unclear to me what is *actually* being cached. I can see from

https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/f57f1301a053485946083d7a45022b278929a78a/setup-renv/action.yaml#L27

that `$HOME/.local/share/renv` is the cache target, but not sure what is in there.

Is this as intended? If so, could you clarify what exactly is being cached and what one should have to do to cache the actual R library to reduce installation time in subsequent GHA runs?

Thanks a lot for your help!

Source of the GHA runs: https://github.com/milanmlft/test-renv-caching/actions

title: Native pipe |> leads to build failure on ubuntu-latest (oldrel-1) even if unevaluated
description:
**Describe the bug**

My package vignette (and I suppose .Rmd files in general) fail to build on `ubuntu-latest (oldrel-1)` if any code chunk uses the new native pipe operator, `|>`. This is not an evaluation error, since the code only executes if it detects R >= 4.1. Rather it is linked to the trailing `>` at the end of a line. 

At first, I suspected it might be because of an older Pandoc version, but I can see that the other OS builds (which all work fine) use the same Pandoc version. I couldn't find anyone else running into this issue online, so I'm a bit stumped.

**To Reproduce**

https://github.com/grantmcdermott/ritest/runs/4084157327?check_suite_focus=true

The offending code chunk is

```
## Only run this code if you have R 4.1 or above
if (getRversion() >= "4.1") {
  feols(yield ~ N + P + K | block, vcov = 'iid', data = npk) |>
  ritest('N', strata = 'block', reps = 1e3, seed = 99L) |>
  plot()
}
```

**Expected behavior**

Either to skip evaluation because an older R release is detected (but still knit the code), or evaluate and display the code+results if using a newer release of R.

title: setup-pandoc does not manage to install properly some recent versions on Windows
description:
I discovered this in **rmarkdown** CI: https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/actions/runs/732459867

When trying to install Pandoc 2.11.4, there was no error in the installation with `setup-pandoc` but it seems the binary is not correctly put in the PATH or installed. 

`rmarkdown::find_pandoc()` can't find it: https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/runs/2304396532?check_suite_focus=true#step:13:144

We know that Pandoc bundles have changed between version. It seems it is handled in the code 
https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/18d8b3cd131edfa357583fc071e138e82abdb0a9/setup-pandoc/src/setup-pandoc.ts#L107-L117

However, I did a quick test with several version an recent one does not installs correctly on windows: 

* 2.13 : https://github.com/cderv/test-actions/runs/2304715568?check_suite_focus=true
* 2.11.4: https://github.com/cderv/test-actions/runs/2304715588?check_suite_focus=true

Currently `setup-pandoc` can't be used with recent Pandoc version to install on Windows it seems.
